items.quote: any new CAPEX what we do, we generally see to it that within three to four years, we have that know, ROI in place.

items.quote: solvent, what happens is solvent, everybody in the industry, depending on their manufacturing capacity, they have a limited storage capacity of solvents. So no one can store solvents for more than 10 to 15 odd days.

items.statement: Coal-based CCPP expected to save INR 10-12 crores per month once operational

items.quote: The EEI, that is Electrical and Electronics Instrumentation segment continued to be the primary growth engine for the group. The EEI segment has registered a growth of 17.5% in FY '26 on a year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Radio industry continued to witness cautious advertiser sentiment during Q4 FY26
items.quote: The radio industry continued to witness cautious advertiser sentiment during the quarter.

items.statement: No current plans for M&A or inorganic opportunities; focusing on organic growth and AI integration

items.statement: Company holding cash reserves with no current deployment plan

items.statement: Most cost efficiencies already actioned and implemented; continuous effort to use technology for further efficiency gains
items.quote: So most of the cost efficiencies have already been actioned and have been implemented, and we are actually seeing that effect from quarter 4 and this year going forward. But there is a continuous effort to look at technology to improve efficiencies.

items.statement: Revenue remained subdued due to softer industry conditions and seasonal moderation in advertiser activity
items.quote: While revenue performance continued to remain subdued due to softer industry conditions, our efforts towards optimizing expenses and enhancing operational efficiencies supported in improving our margins and profitability during the quarter.

items.quote: We have a total of 22 outlets, out of which 14 are New Balance exclusive brand outlets, and 8 are our Sneaker multi-brand stores.

items.statement: CG Premedia revenue doubled to ~Rs 3 crore in FY26 from Rs 1-1.5 crore; remains a business development unit, not a major revenue driver.
items.quote: CG Premedia is a small entity. You should think of it as a business development unit within Creative, Its revenue was around 3 crores for the whole year.

items.statement: Pune center with 3T MRI and cardiac CT expected operational by June 2026

items.statement: Shegaon CT center in 100-bed hospital expected operational June-July 2026

The reason is although our operational income. core trading margin has gone up, but because of there is excess liquidity or I will say sufficient liquidity with the DISCOM, so they are making payment on time and that is why our rebate income actually has gone down from 121 crore to 97 crore during this y

items.statement: Net working capital days reduced from 19 to 8 days; gross debtor days down from 51 to 44 days; recovered ~Rs 1,000 crore from J&K
items.quote: So our net working capital has gone down to 848 crore. In number of days if you will see that our gross debtor days has gone down from 51 days to 44 days and if we exclude the creditors also that is net working capital has gone down from 19 days to 8 days.

items.statement: Net cash position Rs 2,800 crore as of March 31, 2025; approximately Rs 2,400 crore currently
items.quote: Net cash was on 31st March is around 2,800 crore and today should be around 2,400 crore, something like this.

items.statement: PFS divestment process pause removed by board; will seek approvals and move forward; no investment banker appointed yet
items.quote: Now we have to report now that that particular decision to pause is not there. So, which means we can go ahead. Having said that, we divest, we hold in what manner, what is determined to be the best manner in the interest of the shareholders.

items.statement: Trading BESS power with early movers; supplying green power to GAIL Vijaipur 10 MW green hydrogen project; engaging with data centers for round-the-clock green power
items.quote: In terms of the new initiative, we are trading Bess Power. There are two or three early movers in BESS and we are in touch with them and also trading their power. Green hydrogen, we are talking to two, three people to supply electricity and incidentally, I think it was the first at that point of time. Now there is a GAIL Vijaipur green hydrogen project. So we have only supplied green power to it.

items.statement: Over 70 licensed traders compete in short-term/exchange segments; cross-border and long-term limited to 4-6 credible traders; PTC has moat from balance sheet, relationships, cross-border expertise
items.quote: Whereas if you look at power exchange transactions or short term transactions, there we have to compete with almost everybody. So there are more than 70 licensed traders in the country currently. So for those volumes, we have to compete with those 70 traders. All of them are there in the market for that. Whereas cross-border and long-term, if somebody has to enter into a 25-year or a 15-year or a

items.statement: PFS asset quality: distressed assets largely addressed; remaining expected to resolve near term; no further surprises expected beyond public knowledge
items.quote: We do not have any reason to believe that there is any further surprise for us in terms of their quality beside what is already been reported and what is already in the public discourse and knowledge.

items.statement: Teesta Urja dam construction in two phases: cofferdam operational by Sep-Oct 2025 supplying 40-50% capacity; full dam ready by 2029
items.quote: So actually this Teesta Urja will be developed in, as already explained in the last CONCALL also, that it will be constructed in two phases. First they are building a cofferdam. Through that I think that around 40-50% of the total megawatt will be supplied through that. And that should be operational by let's say September or October. And the full dam will be ready by 29 actually.

items.statement: Renewable energy share in India's installed capacity >50% (223 GW); energy generation share up from 16% to 26% in 10 years; target 29% for current year
items.quote: So in terms of installed capacity, the renewable is more than 50% but if we look in energy terms, it has increased from 16% to 26%. So that's not a small jump in the last 10 years. And now in the total energy that is consumed in the country, 26% is coming from the renewables. And the target for this year as far as MNRE and ministries are concerned is actually 29%.

items.statement: Added new clients in C&I space and cross-border domain; consulting for PM Kusum smart meters and rooftop solar; ADB project connecting Laos, Thailand, Cambodia power markets
items.quote: And of course, some new clients have been added across C&I space and also in the cross-border domain. And there are some consultancy assignments which are a little unique and which are helping contribute in this, especially the PM Kusum project of Honourable Prime Minister where we are helping the utilities in smart meter installations and also rooftop solar projects. And lastly the ADB funded pro

items.statement: Renewable purchase obligation targets stiff at 29% for current year driving renewable generation growth
items.quote: And the target for this year as far as MNRE and ministries are concerned is actually 29%. So the targets are very stiff and the generation from renewables is coming in to meet those stiff targets.

items.statement: Cash balances maintained as war chest for strategic investments and business cyclicity; not considered excessive given working capital needs and fixed cost base of ~Rs 100 crore annually
items.quote: Being in this business for over 20 years, 25 years, we somehow see the cyclicity. So, when we are pragmatic, cautious that this business from time to time does need more cash to be performing it well. Second, we have communicated in the past that a part of this is kept away or like a war chest for select investments.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth guidance of 15% YoY; EBITDA guidance deferred to next quarter due to input cost volatility
items.quote: We expect a revenue growth of 15% on a year-on-year basis. However, on EBITDA, we will be able to share the guidance perhaps only by next quarter as the current input cost situation is extremely volatile and difficult to predict.

items.statement: FY27 capex guided at INR 70-75 crores, with INR 45 crores for Bhiwadi facility and INR 25-30 crores for existing business growth
items.quote: CapEx for the year will be between INR 70 crores and INR 75 crores, split as INR 45 crores for the Bhiwadi facility and the balance INR 25 crores to INR 30 crores for growth of the existing business and factories.

items.statement: Bhiwadi facility construction largely complete; machine fitting in June 2026, test runs thereafter, commercial production by end July or early August 2026
items.quote: Regarding construction of the Bhiwadi facility, it is largely complete. We are in the process of fitting out the facility with machines and assembly lines over the course of June 2026, after which there will be test runs and commercial production starting in the end of July 2026 or the beginning of August 2026.

items.statement: Bhiwadi plant revenue potential INR 550 crores at steady state; FY27 revenue from Bhiwadi guided at INR 80 crores vs earlier INR 140 crores estimate
items.quote: Due to the slight delayed commissioning of the facility, we expect a revenue of INR 80 crores in FY27, against an earlier estimated revenue of INR 140 crores in FY27 from Bhiwadi.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin compressed sharply due to 390 bps gross margin impact from raw material cost surge and INR depreciation; expect full price pass-through by June 2026 to restore gross margins to ~24%
items.quote: This sharp reduction is primarily attributed to a sharp surge in raw material costs across categories, driven by disruptions in supply chain due to the war in the Middle East and challenging geopolitical situation. This has impacted gross margins for the quarter by 390 basis points.

items.statement: Price increases of 10-18% undertaken to offset material and labour cost inflation; full transmission expected by June 2026
items.quote: Given the substantial quantum of increase in material and the sudden unexpected increase in labour minimum wage mid-month, we expect that the price transmission to be fully passed on to customers only by June 2026.

items.statement: Polymer basket (30% of input cost) spiked due to crude oil surge and USD-INR depreciation; aluminium also saw sharp increase; 15% of consumption imported
items.quote: all know, the war has led to a sharp Elin Electronics Ltd Q4 FY26 Investor Call 25.05.2026 spike in crude oil prices, which has in turn led to a sharp spike in polymer prices, as well as a sharp depreciation in the USD-INR rate. This combined basket constitutes 30% of our input cost leading to a sharp spike in our RMC cost

items.statement: Fan business grew 67% YoY driven by BLDC ceiling fans and TPW fans; export business restarted in May 2026 after tariff-related stoppage in August 2025
items.quote: We have seen strong growth of 67% in our fans business on a YoY basis. This has primarily been driven by our BLDC ceiling fans and TPW fans business.

items.statement: Lighting segment ex-flashlights declined QoQ but price declines behind us; small price increases undertaken; five new lighting customers added besides Signify; expect double-digit lighting growth in FY27
items.quote: The LED lighting segment, ex flashlights declined from INR 50 crores last quarter to INR 39.5 crores in the current quarter. Price decline is now completely behind us. Small price increases have been undertaken with customers.

items.statement: Working capital at net 59 days in Q4 FY26 vs target of 45 days; inventory days higher due to strategic raw material stocking in March 2026
items.quote: Our working capital position is at net 59 days. Of this, inventory days was higher than anticipated, as we had to stock up on raw material inventory in March 2026, to safeguard against potential shortages due to the challenging geopolitical situation.

items.statement: BIS norms implementation timeline remains September 2026; no relaxation confirmed yet
items.quote: So as of now it is still September 2026. Now whether this itself gets relaxed, we do not know yet. Probably closer to the date we might have an update, but as of now, it is September 2026.

items.statement: Former CEO resigned for better opportunity; no replacement planned; procurement now overseen by family member with existing team in place
items.quote: No. I mean, no known reason to me. What was known is what was disclosed. He found a better opportunity, he moved on. That is what we know. And we don't intend to get a new CEO.

items.statement: Aspirational EBITDA margin 8% but realistic 6-6.5% in normal times; current gross margin ~24% target after price pass-through; lighting gross margin currently ~15% targeting 18-19% in 2-3 months
items.quote: Aspirational would be higher than that. 6%, 6.5% is definitely achievable. Aspirational would be closer to 8%, but when I say 8%, I also say that in the context of your question being aspirational.

items.statement: Chinese pricing remains a mystery; irrational competition seen in lighting segment; INR depreciation makes imports more expensive but China continues to offer lower rates
items.quote: We are not really able to logically work out how it is that they go on kind of offering lower rates to grab business. So Chinese pricing is somewhat of a mystery, I think, definitely to us and a lot of other Indian industry at large.

items.statement: Two-thirds of customers on quarterly price settlement (one quarter lag), one-third on monthly basis; price increases of 10-18% being negotiated
items.quote: With about maybe two-thirds of our customers it is on a quarterly basis. So, the pricing of Jan, Feb, March, for example, is applicable on the April, May, June price settlement. Therefore, there is a lag of a quarter.

items.statement: Geopolitical situation and war in Middle East causing supply chain disruptions, raw material cost spikes, and currency depreciation; minimum wage in Uttar Pradesh increased 26% effective April 2026
items.quote: Further, you would also have read that minimum wage has been revised upwards sharply in Uttar Pradesh resulting in an effective increase of 26% in April versus March. This was done on 14th April 2026 with effect from 1st April 2026.

items.statement: Management expects CX center utilization to exceed 91% by end of Q1 FY27
items.quote: And the utilization levels as it stood on 31st of March was almost 83% and based on the business and books that we see, it is expected to move beyond 91% by the time we end the Quarter 1.

items.statement: Digital video studio investment approved at INR 11 crores for facilities, IT and real estate
items.quote: The investment in the digital video studio is already in the public domain. It is INR 11 crores.

items.statement: CX center capacity expanded by almost 50% with utilization at 83% as of March 31, 2025
items.quote: The second one was that we had expanded our infrastructure for the customer experience center. Now, we increased by almost 50%. And the utilization levels as it stood on 31st of March was almost 83%

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin improved from 13.5% to 15.5% in FY26
items.quote: EBITDA increased by 31.6% to almost INR 55 crores. And in terms of margins, it improved from almost 13.5% to around 15.5%.

items.statement: Revenue seasonality pattern: 40% in first half, 60% in second half driven by festival season and budget exhaustion
items.quote: Typically, 40% of revenue is in the first half and 60% percent is in the second half, and the reason for that is not difficult to fathom. Budgets get, let us say, assembled or determined in Q1 and then we hit the monsoon.

items.statement: Revenue mix approximately 44-45% communications, 25% research, 30% analytics based on standalone entity financials
items.quote: If one was to go with that caveat, and if one was to go with those individual standalone financials, then I would say that almost 44% to 45% of the top line of the income comes from the communication piece, a one-fourth comes from the research piece, and almost 30% thereabouts comes from the analytics piece.

items.statement: Multi-service client revenue share increased to 25-30% of total income from less than 5% previously
items.quote: And clients once they engage with you, they are quite happy to engage with you on other services as well. Why would they go elsewhere? It is from that point of view I think where we had maybe less than 5% of multi-service offerings to a particular client, I think we are at 25%-30% now.

items.statement: 5-year revenue CAGR of 14% from FY21 to FY26, outpacing Sensex (7.6%) and nominal GDP (8-9%)
items.quote: Therefore, if we were to look back, starting from FY21, and going up all the way to FY26, the total income for the company grew at a CAGR of almost 14%.

items.statement: Hired over 600 people in last 12-14 months; employee cost growth managed through muted increments, apprentice hiring, and superannuation exits
items.quote: We have hired over 600 people over the last 12-to 14 months.

items.statement: Positioned as independent homegrown player with speed and relevance advantages over MNC peers undergoing restructuring
items.quote: We are in a quadrant of one. We are on our own trip. We have built capabilities. We believe in this market. I do not write a single e-mail to New York or London or Tokyo to get approvals for anything.

items.statement: AI viewed as productivity tool embedded across workflows; not a displacement threat; 15 AI tools in use in communications alone
items.quote: AI is our tool. I mean, I have 15 in the communication piece only. I think there are 15 tools that are currently in use.

items.statement: Balance sheet remains zero-debt with healthy free cash flow generation
items.quote: The balance sheet continues to remain strong with a zero-debt position and healthy free cash flow generation.

items.statement: Consulting and video studio personnel investments in single-digit crores
items.quote: It is a very measured, Madhur. To answer your question, these are in single-digit crores. They are not large numbers.

items.statement: Capital allocation to remain measured; shareholder returns to be addressed at appropriate time
items.quote: We will not deploy it foolishly. Just because there is cash does not mean we need to go out and spend it. It will be done in a measured way only.

items.statement: FY27 revenue target 70-100% growth with similar profitability; long-term vision INR1,000 cr revenue by 2030 at 12-13% PAT margin
items.quote: I would like to give an outlook for FY27, which approximately I am expecting a target of 70% to 100% revenue growth, we have taken a minimum. And profit margins will also remain with similar profitability.

items.statement: FY27 revenue guidance INR300 cr minimum, Q1 revenue expected INR65-70 cr
items.quote: I am expecting my outlook for 2027 is INR300 crores. That is not going below INR300 crores, this is going to be above INR300 crores.

items.statement: AkikoPay FY27 revenue expected INR50-100 cr, Q1 INR4-5 cr
items.quote: From AkikoPay, I am expecting revenue in the first quarter because AkikoPay is properly indulged with our core business. If seen, I am expecting AkikoPay revenue of INR50 crores to INR100 crores in FY27.

items.statement: Loan business target INR1,000 cr unsecured book by FY27 end from current INR320 cr
items.quote: By FY27, my target is INR1,000 crores of unsecured book. So, the INR400 crores is to be taken to INR1,000 crores.

items.statement: AkikoPay customer targets: 5 lakh by Sep 30, 1 million by Dec 31
items.quote: I am expecting 5 lakh customers by 30th of September and 1 million customers till 31st December.

items.statement: Q4 margin pressure due to branch expansion, tech investment, Dubai geopolitical issues; FY27 PAT margin guided 9-11%
items.quote: If we look at short-term profitability, margins could have been even stronger, but we have consciously invested to build future operating leverage for long-term scale. And some of our margin pressure has come in Dubai operations, there has b een temporary margin pressure due to the current geopolitical situation

items.statement: AkikoPay margins expected to improve to 12-13% via cross-sell; Q1 visibility, full scale Q2-Q3
items.quote: Yes, those margins will improve a lot. We can reach up to 12% to 13%. I am saying that those margins will improve a lot with cross-sales and all engagements.

items.statement: Monthly credit card disbursement 16,000+; monthly loan disbursement run rate INR400 cr+; annualized book INR5,000 cr
items.quote: Currently, we have reached a monthly disbursement run rate of INR400 crores+, which if we count annually, our book has become INR5,000 crores as of today.

items.statement: Unsecured loan book INR320 cr, secured INR80 cr; 80-20 split to remain
items.quote: Unsecured book is INR320 crores, rest is secured book.

items.statement: Branch expansion to 16 branches across India; technology infrastructure investment; AkikoPay development
items.quote: We have worked aggressively on branch infrastructure, technology systems, and Akiko's ecosystem, so that long-term sustainable growth can be built.

items.statement: Workforce 900+ (employees + channel partners); 16 branches across major cities; digital conversion 10% vs 60-80% with physical presence
items.quote: Reflecting this scale-up, our total combined workforce, including employees and channel partners, has now crossed 900+, which is a very strong growth compared to last year.

items.statement: 70% digital sourcing; 60% digital leads fulfilled by ground team, 40% from channel partners; AkikoPay integrating credit cards, loans, insurance, travel, UPI, AI tools
items.quote: Digitally, we are acquiring around 60% of the business. I mean, digital leads come then it goes to our ground, goes to our employees, they close the fulfilment. 40% business comes from our channel partners like builders, CAs, doctors and other co-channel partners.

items.statement: 25 million customer database; AkikoPay 57,000 downloads, 20% active users; targeting employees to drive 3,000-4,000 daily downloads
items.quote: Along with that, we have a database of 25 million customer base over the past years. So we will market them with nominal cost.

items.statement: Customer acquisition cost INR10-15 vs INR250 for Paytm/PhonePe/CRED due to consent-based marketing to existing database
items.quote: Where Paytm, PhonePe or CRED spends around INR250 to acquire a customer, there our cost comes to INR10 to INR15. Because we are not marketing randomly.

items.statement: AkikoPay iOS launch delayed by compliance; now cleared, expected live this month; IRDAI license applied for insurance/mutual funds by August
items.quote: AkikoPay has not been integrated in Apple yet because there were some compliance issues. All those compliance issues have been

items.statement: FY26 receivable days decreased; cash flow from operations INR5 cr; unsecured focus avoids 2-3 month disbursement delays of secured loans
items.quote: FY26 receivable days have decreased and secondly, given your growth, even cash flow from operations has been reduced to INR5 crores.

items.statement: No fund-raising; completed integrations without external investment; building balance sheet without leverage
items.quote: Today we have completed almost all our integrations without any investment, without any fund-raising. And after that also we are at a good profitable margin and going towards scalability.

items.statement: Founder Ankur Gaba to take MD/CEO role in next 1-2 months; employee count 486 (up from 326), channel partners 430 (up from 100)
items.quote: Yes, 100%. Most likely in the next one or two months. I have already spoken with my management. They did agreed. So, we'll take a -- we'll take a decision very soon and in the next quarter, you will see me as an

items.statement: Q4 revenue INR57.7 cr (+48% YoY), EBITDA INR7.9 cr, PAT +30% YoY; FY26 revenue INR172.6 cr vs INR150 cr vision, PAT margin 10.3%
items.quote: In Q4, our revenue from operations has been INR57.7 crores, which is a 48% year-on-year growth. And EBITDA is INR7.9 crores. And PAT approximately has grown by 30%.

items.statement: FY26 revenue 126% growth, EBITDA 117% growth, PAT 120% growth; EPS doubled from 7.56 to 14.3
items.quote: And there has been a growth of 126% in revenue. And EBITDA has also grown by 117%. And PAT has also grown by 120%.

items.statement: Dubai revenue dropped from INR2-2.5 cr peak to INR50 lakh in Feb, recovered to INR1 cr in April, targeting INR1.25 cr in May; geopolitical risk around Iran region
items.quote: some of our margin pressure has come in Dubai operations, there has b een temporary margin pressure due to the current geopolitical situation, as you all know, around the Iran region

items.statement: AkikoPay iOS compliance risk resolved; Google Play Store download count fluctuation (50k to 10k display) being investigated
items.quote: Now compliance has also been completed, so most likely within this month, everything will be live.

items.statement: AkikoPay 1% cashback strategy sustainable for 1 year with 1.8% MDR and zero acquisition cost; 10-12% users opt for full KYC (2 lakh limit)
items.quote: Sir, this sustainability for next one year will be live because right now we are getting around 1.8% MDR and we are not putting any expense to acquire customer.

items.statement: FY27 revenue guidance INR330-350 crore standalone
items.quote: So, overall, we are anticipating we should be closing somewhere between INR330 crores to INR335 crores to INR350 crores.

items.statement: FY27 gross margin target minimum 15%
items.quote: we are anticipating that that should improve to 15% at a minimum.

items.statement: Flux-cored wire FY27 revenue expectation INR20 crore
items.quote: this year we are expecting somewhere if the industry improves and we see the demand again rising, so somewhere between INR20 odd crores is what we are expecting the flux-cored wire should contribute in this financial year.

items.statement: ERC business to start July, FY27 revenue INR30-35 crore
items.quote: that business will give us a revenue of on a annual basis almost like INR50 crores. So, even if we start somewhere in the month of July, so we expect at least between INR30 crores to INR35 crores coming from ERC business.

items.statement: FY26 gross margin 12.8%, down from 14.6%
items.quote: However, I can see that our gross margins dipped from 14.6% to 12.8% in this financial year.

items.statement: Trading margins very low, manufacturing margins higher
items.quote: Trading is something which we are doing it whenever -- because we try and take benefit of bulk procurement and we trade at relatively very low margins.

items.statement: ERC gross margin 25-28%
items.quote: ERC, the gross margins are relatively healthy, somewhere between 25% to 28% odd is the gross margin there.

items.statement: FY26 manufacturing 73%, trading 27% vs 67/33 last year
items.quote: The mix between manufacturing and trading this year is approximately 67% gross from manufacturing -- sorry 73% gross from manufacturing and 27% gross from trading, against 67% and 33% of last year.

items.statement: FY27 trading share expected below 20%
items.quote: In FY27, we are seeing -- because our -- the growth will come from the manufacturing segment, what we are projecting for this financial year. So, there's a -- it will drop down to less than 20%, the trading sales.

items.statement: Installed capacity: electrodes 10,600 MT, MIG wire 10,600 MT, flux-cored 2,500 MT
items.quote: Our installed production capacity currently stands at 10,600 metric tons for electrodes, 10,600 metric tons for MIG wire across West Bengal and Haryana facilities, and 2,500 metric tons for flux-cored wire.

items.statement: Flux-cored utilisation ~15% in FY26, peak revenue INR30 crore at 100%
items.quote: if you see the split, like last year flux wire has contributed nearly INR4 crores plus to the top line. So, when we see in terms of capacity utilization, it was at almost I think say 15%. Okay, and this year, obviously, whatever initial challenges were there, so that we have been able to overcome. And now we see this year should be, as I had mentioned in my earlier call, that on an optimum level a

items.statement: Debottlenecking and automation to improve throughput and utilisation
items.quote: We have also undertaken ongoing debottlenecking and automation initiatives across our manufacturing facilities, aimed at im proving throughput, operational efficiency, and capacity utilization

items.statement: Operational efficiency capex can push electrode capacity beyond 100% utilisation
items.quote: So, 85%, we had in fact mentioned that we have invested in capex for improving the operational efficiency. So, with the improvement in the operational efficiency, we can even cross your -- the capacity for electrodes.

items.statement: H2 FY26 sales impacted by war in last 15 days of March
items.quote: in the month of March, because of the war, so in the last 15 days, we actually basically saw an impact in terms of turnover.

items.statement: Direct wagon builder demand seeing resistance, dealer network stable
items.quote: We are basically seeing some pressure here, but as far as like your -- when it comes through dealer distribution network, so that business is not impacted so much. But when it comes to direct supplies to wagon builders, wagon manufacturers, there we are seeing a bit of resistance.

items.statement: Significant reduction in short-term borrowings strengthened balance sheet
items.quote: Another important achievement during FY26 was the significant red uction in short -term borrowings, which has further strengthened our balance sheet and liquidity position, providing greater financial flexibility for future growth initiatives

items.statement: Sales mix ~50-55% dealer distribution, 45-50% direct B2B
items.quote: See, it's a mix of like as I said B2B and B2C. The mix is somewhere between 50% -- 55% is from dealer distribution or it's other way to -- from direct to direct end consumers. So, you can say 45/55, somewhere -- sometime it is 50/50.

items.statement: Direct Railways contribution low 5-10%
items.quote: See, we are as government, non-government, largely our sales is to either wagon manufacturers who are in turn supplying to Railways, but direct Railways, like the contribution is low. It may be 5% to 10%.

items.statement: Invested INR1.8-1.9 crore in associate HM Power (14-15% stake) for bank capital requirement
items.quote: So, if you look at what is the quantum of that related party transaction in terms of because there's a investment which has been made in another company by the name HM Power, which is our associate company. So, the investment is I think less than INR1 crore. I think INR1.8 crores or INR1.9 crores is only the amount which has been invested in that company.

items.statement: HM Power associate FY27 revenue expected INR200 crore, Classic owns 14-15%
items.quote: Out of that company, in this current financial year, we are expecting a revenue of INR200 crores.

items.statement: Margin guidance contingent on war situation normalising
items.quote: Again, it'll all depend how the global situation, how the global war -- the war between U.S. and Iran subsides or where it leads to, because every day we see something new coming up. So, I think everything has a positive or a negative impact because of the global situation.

items.statement: Commitment to quarterly business updates and announcements
items.quote: Otherwise, definitely we'll share at least quarter-on-quarter what is our revenue growth, what we had shared in Q3, we will continue doing that.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth target of 25-30% minimum with similar margins
items.quote: We aim to grow by 25% to 30% minimum in FY '27 with similar margins.

items.statement: PAT margin expected around 14% in FY27
items.quote: See we will be maintaining the PAT of around 14% approximately.

items.statement: INR 25 crores capex incurred in FY26
items.quote: During the year, we incurred INR25 crores in capital expenditure, reflecting our continuous investment in infrastructure and capabilities.

items.statement: IPO proceeds reallocation of INR 10 crores to nutraceutical facility expansion
items.quote: The board has approved a reallocation of INR 10 crores, primarily from surplus amounts across the veterinary facility , home care, and cosmetic divisions , towards the enhanced construction cost for the nutraceutical CDMO facility.

items.statement: New 75,000 sq ft facility expected operational by July-August 2026, increasing installed capacity 2.5x
items.quote: Our most significant ongoing initiative is the development of a new facility , approximately 75,000 square feet of ground plus four floor structure , expected to become operational by or August 2026. Upon commissioning, this expansion is anticipated to increase our overall installed capacity by approximately 2.5 times the existing

items.statement: Pet care capacity to reach 25 tons/month in 2-3 months; extrusion line upgrade from 100-150 kg/hr to 1000 kg/hr ordered
items.quote: In pet care, our current output stands at around 16 to 18 tons per month with a near term capacity expected to reach to 25 tons per month within the next two to three months. We have also ordered a high-capacity pet food extrusion line, upgrading from our 100-150 kg per hour to 1000 kg per hour to support the long term growth demand.

items.statement: Beverage canning facility planned at 10,000 bottles/hour with Tetra pack line booked
items.quote: We are building out a canning facility and a carbonated beverage line with a Tetra pack line already booked. Plan ned installed capacity is approximately 10,000 bottles per hour.

items.statement: Client base of 718+ with 98% retention rate
items.quote: On the client front, we have served a base of 718 plus clients with a retention rate of 98% , reflecting the strength of our long term relationships and consistency of product quality.

items.statement: New clients added including Nykaa, Khandelwal Labs, Aristo
items.quote: We have good orders, we have a good client base. We have started a lot of new companies are rolled in with good names like Nykaa, Khandelwal Labs. There are many good names that have joined. Aristo is there.

items.statement: Protein and snack bar demand more than doubled
items.quote: The protein and snack bar line sub segment also witnessed a strong growth with demand more than doubling.

items.statement: Export growth at 10-15% annually; international markets to be increasingly meaningful
items.quote: Export growth continues at 10% to 15% annually and we expect international markets to be an increasingly meaningful contributor going forward.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin expanded 72 bps to 20.3%; PAT margin expanded 129 bps to 14%
items.quote: With full year EBITDA margin expanding by 72 bps to 20.3%. PAT stood at around INR10.5 crores for H2 FY '26 u p by 38% year-on-year, bringing full year FY PAT to INR20.5 crores with full year PAT margin expanding by 129 bps points to 14%.

items.statement: Gross margin dip in H2 due to packaging and raw material cost increases with lag in pass-through

items.statement: FY26 operating revenue grew 88% YoY to Rs 57.26 crore with H2 revenue of Rs 27.8 crore, up 53% YoY

items.statement: Customer base expanded from 100 to 10,000+ across 100+ countries in two years; Socify added 100 case-study customers in six months
items.quote: We delivered 10,000 plus client base across TAC and Cyberscope footprint expanded across 100 plus countries. That's biggest achievement, I would say, ever in cybersecurity history, not just in India, but globally.

items.quote: Today, where we used to spend 5 to 10 days on smart contract audit, that can happen in just 5 minutes on Cyberscopes AI, which we launched last week. So things have been great.

items.statement: Key enterprise customers include Microsoft, Google, Apple, Meta, SAP, Autodesk, Anthropic; 70% revenue from Western geographies
items.quote: We work for Microsoft, we work for Google, we work for today, I want to address a couple of more things. We work for SAP, we work for Autodesk, right? So we have a...Customer base, we're getting as a vendor.

items.quote: When we acquired the company, it was approximately 8 people. Today they are 28. So we are investing into technology. We are investing into enterprise version of the solution.

items.statement: Over 80% of FY26 total revenue already collected; platform model avoids long government sales and collection cycles
items.quote: Out of 57 crore of the total revenue, already more than 80% has been already received. We are not working for the government where, you know, the sales cycle is for one year, then again, the collection delivery cycle is one year.

items.statement: EBITDA margin 53.8% exceeds global peers Qualys, Checkpoint, Fortinet, Palo Alto, Zscaler; operating leverage maintained with revenue and profit growing at same pace

items.statement: Biax division revenue flat at INR140-142 crores in FY26 due to capacity constraints

items.statement: Aggregate production volume declined 5% to 31,335 MT in FY26 from 33,014 MT
items.quote: Aggregate production volume declined 5% to 31,335 metric tons from 33,014 metric tons.

items.statement: Net revenue declined 5.6% to INR505.5 crores in FY26 from INR535.28 crores
items.quote: Net revenues were INR505.5 crores, down 5.6% from the INR535.28 crores in the previous year.

items.statement: All warrants converted, 11.7 lakh shares allotted; INR74.63 crores held in banks pending deployment from preferential issue and QIP

items.statement: FY27 revenue guidance of INR700 crores
items.quote: So FY27, we are sticking to our guidance of INR700 crores. For that, we have to do our best to raise funds either through equity or debt.

items.statement: Target PAT margin of 9-10% sustainable, aiming to regain 11-11.5%
items.quote: So we will be trying to maintain this because I think this is the worst scenario that we have faced. So we are trying to ensure that 9% - 10% of PAT will always be maintained.

items.statement: EBITDA margin of 18-20% considered sustainable
items.quote: And the operating margins, EBITDA margins about 18% to 20% is workable, given the rise in the fuel prices, etc. Prasanna D.: Yes, it will be sustainable, and it will be workable

items.statement: Current unexecuted order book around INR500 crores
items.quote: It's roughly around INR500 crores. We have started bidding after the elections are over, we will try to increase our order book to a phase where we'll be able to achieve it in the next year

items.statement: Headcount to increase proportionally with revenue growth

items.statement: Bitumen price hike 50-60% impacted margins; price escalation clauses exist for projects >12 months
items.quote: But when a price hike of around 50% or 60% happened in the raw material, that too in the bitumen, which is a major raw material in road laying, will definitely have a hit.

items.statement: Price escalation clauses apply only for projects >12 months; state govt caps at 5% variation
items.quote: There are some works that, if we are bidding on a tender that is less than a year, that was not covered in the price escalation clause. Only if the duration of the work is more than 12 months, that is, 13 months or more, will price escalation be there.

items.statement: Trade receivables INR160 crores, collected INR55-60 crores in Apr-May; inventory INR15-20 crores
items.quote: Out of INR140 crores, we have done around INR55 crores to INR60 crores to date. And in this console thing, another INR5 crores or something we have received.

items.statement: Ind AS adoption expected to reduce inventory days by recognizing unbilled revenue
items.quote: Once we start following Ind AS, unbilled will become a part of revenue itself, sir. So inventory days will automatically come down because, sir, our inventory is somewhere in the range from INR15 crores to INR20 crores, actually, not more than that.

items.statement: Consolidated debt INR234 crores; standalone INR206 crores (CC INR140 cr, term loan INR48-50 cr, promoter loan INR15-18 cr)
items.quote: If you just concentrate on the standalone, our total debt is coming somewhere INR206 crores in the standalone. I'll just give a small bifurcation on this. Out of this INR206 crores, we have INR140 crores as CC limit with our banks

items.statement: NHAI bidding very competitive; management remains conservative on pricing
items.quote: When we come into this NHAI bidding, the price has to be much more competitive. Now that prices are very competitive in the market, people are ready to go for higher prices. We are very conservative in this.

items.statement: Government issued circular on escalation clauses due to geopolitical tensions
items.quote: As these escalation clauses, the government have come up with some notifications and because of this geopolitical tension, the government has come up with a circular for the escalation clauses, explaining how things have to be followed

items.statement: Cash flow from operations negative for 3 years; working capital funded by debt/equity
items.quote: We do not claim that we have been operationally positive for the past 3 years. For a growing company like us, you cannot expect 100% operationally positive things. We are trying our level best to bring it to an operationally positive.

items.statement: Unbilled revenue INR80 crores in March due to milestone billing delays
items.quote: We have a high unbilled revenue of around INR80 crores, which we couldn't bill during February and March. The problem is that in accounts, you have to follow the accrual system and book all the expenses.

items.statement: No increase in promoter salary; employee cost rise due to project site hiring
items.quote: Whatever increase in employee cost you are seeing, it is all because we have hired people for our project sites and all. There is no increase in promoter salary in any way.

items.statement: Promoter may buy back shares instead of diluting at low price
items.quote: I will instead buy back myself.

items.statement: Targets INR700 crore revenue for current year and INR850-900 crore for next year
items.quote: Let's say, if we are doing INR700 crores for this year, we may be targeting INR850 crores to INR900 crores for next year as well and things like that.

items.statement: Expects INR500-1000 crore new orders this year on top of current unexecuted order book
items.quote: Apart from the current unexecuted order book, we are expecting around INR500 crores plus this year also. So anything between INR500 crores and INR1,000 crores, we are trying to have it in our order book kitty.

items.statement: Planning equity raise before end of Q2 FY27
items.quote: And about the equity raise, we are planning something before end of Q2 to happen, sir.

items.statement: Shifting to IndAS this financial year to improve working capital cycle; unbilled revenue will become part of revenue
items.quote: We are shifting into IndAS, sir. After that, you will not see this much of a gap in working capital.

items.quote: Considering the debtor days, whatever it is for a company performing INR1,000 crores, we can take at least INR200 crores to INR250 crores, that can be INR250 crores at least to be in this unbilled revenue, or I mean debtor trade receivables.

items.statement: Targets trade receivables below 15% of revenue (INR150-200 crore at INR1000 crore) and trade payables 10-12%
items.quote: I'll be happy if the trade receivables are maintained well below 15% of our top line, maybe around INR150 crores or INR200 crores if the top line is at INR1,000 crores.

items.statement: EBITDA margin 19.32% in H2; targets 20%+ if bitumen prices stabilize
items.quote: Sir, definitely. Sir, we are right now 19.32% , actually. And I also said why our EBITDA was lower. So, we'll definitely try , sir, if prices and all are good, like a geopolitical reason, our bitumen prices went up. But I'm sure, sir, this time, it will be 20% and above only, sir.

items.statement: Short-term borrowings include INR50-51 crore term loan for vehicles and machinery to be repaid this financial year
items.quote: The remaining INR50 crores, INR51 crores is actually term loan, which we have taken for our vehicle and machinery, which we are going to repay in this financial year.

items.statement: Receivables split approximately 60% NHAI, 40% state government
items.quote: Sir, exact percentage, I don't remember, but we usually maintain 60 -40, sir, like 60% NHAI, 40% state government , like that.

items.quote: Now they have introduced something , like they have instructed all the regional offices to calculate the escalations on a running account basis, so that it will be easier for the contractors.

items.statement: Maximum technical capacity INR400-500 crore per order; currently targeting INR100 crore minimum orders
items.quote: The maximum is around INR400 crores to INR500 crores , and the minimum, we are targeting at INR100 crores or something.

items.statement: May consider bill discounting if cash crunch arises; confident of equity raise and warrant exercise to reduce debt
items.quote: If we at all have to face that cash crunch at all, we'll make sure that the receivables are there within this cycle of what we are maintaining. And also, we might go for discounting of debtors, which we have not done till now.

items.statement: Recruited special tendering team in last 2 months to bid on 100+ tenders for higher win probability
items.quote: So, what we have decided is instead of bidding for 10 tenders and getting 2 tenders, we have decided to go bid for 100 tenders so that the probability will be much higher. So, we have recruited a special team in the last 2 months so that they keep on working on all the tenders that are positive for us.

items.statement: Trade payables flat at INR20 crore despite 4x revenue growth from INR115 crore to INR420 crore over 3 years
items.quote: In financial year '25, our trade payable was standing somewhere INR16 crores, where we had a top line of INR272 crores. In financial year '26, we're having a top line of INR420 crores, stand- alone and the trade payable stand -alone, I'm talking to you, is around INR20 crores, sir.

items.statement: NHAI and state officials discussing VG30 bitumen substitution for VG40 to ease supply constraints
items.quote: VG40 is a problematic thing. So, what the NHAI and other state officials are now on the talks to get it done with VG30 itself. VG30 and VG40 are not much of a difference. So, they are planning to have the conditions not restricted to VG40 and where they may implement VG30.

items.statement: No political party linkages; rumors stem from brother-in-law being actor and new CM Vijay also being actor
items.quote: I don't have any link with any political parties except for two days. One day, I'll vote for the State election, one day for the Central election. items.statement: Conceptia projects 20% growth, Waveoptix projects ~30% growth for FY27
items.quote: So these two companies also, both Conceptia and Waveoptix, as per their projection, they will also be growing; Conceptia at about 20%, and Waveoptix at about close to 30 odd%.

items.statement: Seeing raw material cost increases in steel and fuel but not substantial margin impact
items.quote: Yes, we are. So it's a global issue that is there. So how could we be insulated? There is going to be an uptake in terms of fuel costs, in steel prices, all of that. So that definitely, there is an uptake in that. There is going to be an increase in the raw material pricing, increase the conversion cost per se.

items.statement: Inventory dropped to INR163 crore at year-end due to timing; average inventory ~INR40 crore
items.quote: The inventory is just a cut off on that particular date. Our raw materials that were to come in February and March have come in first week of April that is there. But if you saw the average inventory holding that is there, Krishna Defence & Allied Industries Limited Q4 & FY26 Post Earnings Conference Call May 22, 2026 that was in the range of about INR40 odd crore rupees

items.statement: Cash balance north of INR100 crore including INR65 crore liquid reserves in long-term FDs
items.quote: Yeah, I couldn't unmute sorry. Yeah, yeah, that helps sir. So just trying to understand, so our cash balance is sitting at north of INR100 crore right now. Would that be fair to say? Manish Shah: Yes, you are right. In ball park, you are right.

items.statement: Bulb bar and weld consumables classified; not allowed to export
items.quote: The steels that we are doing for the Bulb bar, for the Navy or the weld consumable, these are all classified. So we are not allowed to export the same as we speak.

items.statement: AUV development with Navy/DRDO and NIO Goa ToT; Indian Navy earmarked ~$1 billion for autonomous underwater platforms
items.quote: The Navy has earmarked in budget about close to $1 billion on the autonomous or AUV space that is there.

items.statement: Expects to reach around 65% capacity utilization by end of current fiscal year (FY27)
items.quote: broadly we anticipate that by the end of the current fiscal year, we should reach around 65% capacity utilization.

items.statement: Targets 30-35% export revenue share over next three years
items.quote: broadly we see that in next three years Neochem's target is that we should have 30-35% revenue coming from exports.

items.statement: Aims to bring trade receivables to around 120 days by H1 FY27 or latest by end of FY27
items.period: H1 FY27 or end of FY27
items.quote: we aim to bring it to a round 120 days, maybe by H1 FY27 or latest by the end of FY27.

items.statement: Believes sustainable margins are 35% gross, 18-20% EBITDA, 10-12% PAT for current product mix
items.quote: we believe these margins are sustainable for this kind of product mix and the industries that we currently cater to, around 35% gross margin, around 18% to 20% EBITDA margin, and around 10% to 12% PAT margin.

items.statement: Expects operating cash flow to normalize by current fiscal year-end (FY27)
items.quote: Broadly by the current fiscal year-end, it would be quite healthier than what it is today.

items.statement: No major planned capex over next 1.5-2 years; only minor equipment additions for formulations
items.quote: we will not require any major planned capex over the next one -and-a-half to two years. However, ours is a formulation -driven business wherein certain formulations may require a couple of equipment additions or some lab testing equipment, which is an ongoing requirement for any manufacturing company.

items.statement: Installed capacity 22,000 MTPA; utilization improved from 35% in FY24 to 53% in FY26 with 47% headroom
items.quote: Over the last few years, capacity utilization has steadily improved from approximately 35% in FY24 to 53% in FY26. As utilization levels continue to improve, we expect to benefit from stronger fixed cost absorption and operating leverage, supporting sustainable margin expansion over time.

items.statement: Delivered 26% volume growth and 32% value growth in FY26
items.quote: So we delivered exactly 26% volume growth year-on-year and 32% value growth.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expanded 321 bps to 20.4% in FY26 driven by favorable product mix, higher utilization, operating leverage, cost discipline
items.quote: EBITDA margin expanded by 321 basis points to 20.4% compared to 17.2% in the previous year. The improvement in profitability was driven by a combination of favorable product mix, higher capacity utilization, operating leverage benefits, and continued cost discipline across the business.

items.statement: Raw material cost remained broadly aligned with revenue growth; 30% of raw materials directly crude-linked; passed on price increases to customers during West Asia crisis
items.quote: Raw material cost remained broadly aligned with the revenue growth, reflecting a relatively stable input cost environment during the year.

items.statement: Shifted from 75% white-label in FY22 to >80% own-brand in FY26; targeting bio-based esters and silicones to contribute 55-60% of revenue in 2 years
items.quote: We would like these two categories to contribute around 55% to 60% of our total revenu e over the next two years.

items.statement: Textile share fell from 85% in FY25 to <75% in FY26; targets <50% in 3 years while HPC grew from 2% in FY24 to 14% in FY26
items.quote: in FY22 we were 100% into textiles, in FY25 we came down to 85%, and in FY26 we concluded at less than 75%. Going forward, over the next three years, while we will continue to grow in textiles, the textile contribution should come down to below 50% of the total revenue.

items.statement: Business model shifted from white-label to own-brand via distribution partners; adding direct corporate customers; exclusive South Asia partner for Lamoral Coatings with Southeast Asia expansion pending
items.quote: We are exclusive partners for Lamoral for the entire region.

items.statement: Exports 5% of FY26 revenue across 12 countries; Bangladesh ~20% of FY25 exports; targeting South Asia, Southeast Asia, Africa; North America and Europe opportunistic
items.quote: Exports currently account for around 5% of our revenue of FY26 and we believe that this represents a significant long-term opportunity.

items.statement: Trade receivables INR48 cr (~160 days) elevated due to Q4 seasonality (32% of annual revenue); 35%+ of FY26 receivables collected by May; payables down due to MSME mandates and war-related inventory procurement
items.quote: Quarter four itself contributed over 32% of our annual revenue. So the figure that you see in the books, which is around INR48 crores as trade receivables, reflects a weighted average of around 160 days.

items.statement: Long-term borrowings reduced from INR14.3 cr to INR0.7 cr in FY26 using IPO proceeds; debt-to-equity improved from 1.8 to 0.2; short-term borrowings INR17.1 cr for working capital
items.quote: Long-term borrowings were substantially reduced to just INR0.7 crores in FY26 from INR14.3 crores FY25. This reflects our disciplined approach to capital allocation and our decision to utilize a portion of IPO proceeds towards repayment of legacy debt

items.statement: IPO proceeds used for legacy debt repayment; balance sheet significantly strengthened
items.quote: This reflects our disciplined approach to capital allocation and our decision to utilize a portion of IPO proceeds towards repayment of legacy debt

items.statement: R&D spend ~2% of revenue historically and in FY26; targeting 2-3% for current year, then need-based
items.quote: R&D spend was around 2% of our revenue, and broadly FY26 also closed at around 2%. We would like to maintain it in the range of around 2% to 3% for this year.

items.statement: West Asia crisis impact partially hedged via inventory and price pass-through; bio-based esters provide partial crude hedge but logistics/utilities exposed; war continuation could impact projections within +/-10% variance
items.quote: with a plus-minus 10% variance, we still fee l that our numbers and projections should remain intact if the war continues.

items.statement: Employee cost peaked from FY21 strategic hiring; team built before revenue scale; minimal inflationary growth due to attrition balancing additions
items.quote: So we had incurred a significant employee cost from FY21 onwards, wherein the results started becoming visible from FY23. So once you have the team in place, you do not need to keep adding more and more people.

items.statement: MSME payment mandates reduced trade payables days from 117 to 56; Europe REACH compliance a barrier; awaiting FTA clarity for Europe expansion
items.quote: Since the Government of India has MSME payment mandates, naturally we have to clear a significant amount of MSME payments towards the end of the year, and that is one impact.

items.statement: Benefiting from MNC consolidation in textile chemicals; Indian players with right products/services gaining share; Lamoral partnership brings fluorine-free tech as PFAS regulations tighten globally
items.quote: there has been a lot of consolidation in multinational companies, wherein Indian companies that are providin g the right products and right services are getting significant benefits.

items.statement: Broad-based demand across portfolio and end-user industries drove 32% revenue growth; HPC and paints/coatings identified as key growth drivers alongside textiles
items.quote: Revenue from operations for FY26 stood at INR110.7 crores, representing a growth of 32% year -on-year, driven by broad -based demand across our product portfolio and end-user industries.

items.statement: Intends to move to quarterly reporting after H1 FY27 review; currently half-yearly as SME listing
items.quote: We will review it after H1.

items.statement: FY28 and beyond targets not set yet; only FY27 visibility provided
items.quote: Not yet. No, those targets are not set yet. As of now, I cannot even say anything about FY '28. So we can only talk about FY '27 today.

items.statement: Offshore revenue INR75-80 crores yearly, port revenue INR12-15 crores yearly; oil spill response flattening as contracts end

items.quote: On an average basis, we can add INR12 crores to INR15 crores from the port business. And from the offshore business, we can add around INR75 crores to INR80 crores, yearly?

items.value: INR8-9 crores/month season; INR4 crores/month off-season
items.quote: See, currently, we are totally doing about INR8 crores to INR9 crores on a monthly basis. This is in the month of the season business. In the off-season, it will decrease by about INR4 crores per month

items.quote: So the raising of preferential was for -- not only for buying new vessels, but also for repayment of our high-cost loans. So we have done that to whatever we have promised. And so up to approximately INR5 crores to INR6 crores, we have already repaid in March 2026

In the port services and oilfield response, it will be about 6.5 years, seven years right

items.statement: Not buying vessels speculatively despite peer expansion; asset prices high due to Gulf crisis; will only purchase with confirmed contracts
items.quote: So we -- as a company, we find that the -- because the market pricing is very high for assets as of today, we do not want to get caught in a high asset value and then get stuck in it because when we buy an asset, we have to buy it for the next 10 to 15 years at least.

items.statement: DG circulars pushing fleet renewal at 20 years vs previous 25 years; electric tug tenders from Mumbai/Kolkata/Chennai ports not commercially viable at current capex
items.quote: So we typically tend to change the fleet after 25 years, but there have been recent DG circulars, which are asking us to basically, the government is asking the owners to renew the fleet at a younger age, say, about 20 years right now.

items.statement: FY26 net profit INR14.72 crores (+25%), EPS INR9.13 (+11.5%), revenue flat INR97.55 crores
items.value: INR14.72 crores PAT; INR97.55 crores revenue
items.quote: Our net profit actually grew by 25% to INR14.72 crores, and our earnings grew by -- earnings per share grew 11.5% to INR9.13. Revenue, however, was broadly flat as compared to last year at INR97.55.

items.statement: JV with UPG Group (26% stake) for shipbuilding/repair/offshore supply base in Odisha; SPV United Sadhav Integrated Maritime formed; land identified, awaiting government allocation
items.quote: We have also formed an SPV joint venture company between the UPG group and Sadhav Shipping Ltd which is named as United Sadhav Integrated Maritime Private Limited, in which Sadhav is a 26% joint venture partner.

items.statement: Electric tug capex too high vs 15-year annuity charter rates; not participating in tenders until economics improve
items.quote: We do not believe that -- or rather we are of the firm belief that the capex for the electric boat is too high as of today. Unless it comes down, the expected charter rate on the annuity basis for 15 years is not making commercial sense.

items.statement: No specific working capital metrics discussed; focus on cost mitigation and confirmed revenue contracts
items.quote: We are also looking at how to mitigate those. Yeah. And then we are also -- the new businesses that are supposed to come in are getting delayed because of this geopolitical crisis actually.

items.statement: Q4 domestic net sales grew 9.2% year-on-year with broad-based growth across Core, Premium, Toothpaste, Toothbrush and Personal Care
items.quote: We have seen over the last quarter a significant acceleration in net sales growth for Q4, our domestic growth now at 9.2%.

items.statement: Q4 gross margin at 69.6% and EBITDA margin a shade over 32%, described as best in class
items.quote: Gross margins continue to be strong at 69.6% and EBITDA margins continue to be absolutely best in class at a shade over 32%.

items.statement: Expect urban markets to continue seeing growth off a soft base; rural to grow faster than urban but not as far ahead as in 2025; overall market flat-to-increasing

items.quote: Our plants now get tracked automatically by the digital twin, where there is a twin that runs alongside the main plant and allows us to be proactive in terms of our actions and also make sure that efficiency and throughput remain at the top of the pile.

items.statement: Colgate Strong Teeth clinically proven 8.5x more effective at re-mineralizing than competition
items.quote: Strong Teeth is 8.5x more effective at re-mineralizing, which is really what prevents you from getting cavities and building the strength of your enamel than the competition.

items.quote: Given the impact of GST on pricing from September-October of last year, we really do need to take a continuous look at volume growth because the value growth pickup that you get in Nielsen will be quite distorted, given that MRP pricing has actually gone down.

items.quote: What we found out of this is that we are significantly able to move attitude by about 7%, get 7% delta in terms of people brushing once, and a significant delta in terms of claimed brushing twice.

items.statement: Entering Calendar Year 2026 with renewed optimism and confidence in consistent long-term growth delivery

items.quote: We have a Harry Potter range that's going to hit shelves very, very soon, so this is a sneak peek, not yet available.

items.statement: Distribution inventory continues to be exceptionally well-managed and decreasing as forecasting gets more efficient
items.quote: Distribution inventory continues to be exceptionally well-managed, and we actually keep decreasing it as we get more efficient and as forecasting gets more efficient.

items.statement: Whitening segment growing 4x faster than overall Toothpaste category; 42% of Indians want whiter teeth

items.quote: The margin performance remains roughly in line with what you are seeing for Q4. And profitability also remains slightly challenged given that the top line growth has been flat.

items.quote: GST provided us a real opportunity to make sure that we could do the Rs. 10 brush, and we have capitalized on it.

items.statement: Urban consumer replaces toothbrush once in 6 months; rural consumer as slowly as once in 15 months; new brush cleans 95% better than old
items.quote: On average, the urban consumer replaces his or her Toothbrush once in six months. Rural consumers replace their Toothbrush as slowly as once in 15 months. And a new Toothbrush cleans 95% better than an old, frayed, flared Toothbrush.

items.quote: E-commerce as a channel is growth-accretive, margin-accretive, share-accretive, premiumization-accretive for us, which is absolutely fantastic because as e-commerce grows, we tend to do better and better.

items.quote: Different categories will see different pricing. Depends on the cost increases we are seeing. But it will be in the low single digit.

items.statement: E-commerce channel ~10% of business, growing faster, gaining share, driving premiumization and margin accretion

items.quote: We have functional academies which are building technical expertise up and down the organization, whether it is sales, whether it's our professional field force, whether it is supply chain, it doesn't matter. items.quote: as per that guidance, our revenue should exceed in this year by Rs.3,000 crores, but we are upbeat that with our cell line which is going to be operational in the next 90-days, so our numbers should exceed our guidance by a reasonable. margin.

items.statement: 4-year revenue CAGR: Rs 194 crore (FY23) to Rs 2,223 crore (FY26) = 11.44x; EBITDA 26x; PAT 54x; EBITDA margin 6.5% to ~15%

items.quote: Cell line will come after the start of the phase. Definitely, we will achieve that with the copper paste. EBITDA Margins will improve now, but let the lines first start.

items.quote: We have entered into the partnership with TotalEnergies in November'25. This partnership enable us to jointly work towards offshore seismic program design data, interpreting and evaluating the opportunities across prospective areas.

items.statement: Highest ever drilling: 74 wells (22 exploratory, 52 development); 307 workovers; highest daily crude production in decade at 81,354 bpd
items.quote: Our highest daily crude oil production in the last decade of around 81,354 barrels per day. We have drilled 74 wells, the highest ever drilling performance in a single year, and We have completed 307 well workover, which is again a record for us.

items.statement: Mozambique LNG force majeure lifted Nov 2025; 6,000 people on site; two 13 MMTPA trains targeting commissioning end-2028/early-2029
items.quote: Effective November 2025, the force majeure which was there earlier in Mozambique project has been removed, there are about 6,000 people on the ground, and we are now looking at the two trains, two LNG trains of 13 MMTPA getting commissioned end 2028 or early 2029.

items.statement: Economic blockade in operating area caused loss of 0.1 MMT crude and 0.3 BCM gas in FY26
items.quote: Because of that, the production took a hit. So, we lost an opportunity of about 0.1 million metric ton of crude oil and about 0.3 million BCM of natural gas.

items.statement: Deep water exploration capability being built via training, ONGC facilities, consultants; field development capability needed post-discovery
items.quote: Should there be a discovery, of course, we would require additional capability in terms of deep-water field development. But as far as exploration technique is concerned, Oil India is fully capable.

items.statement: NRL expansion commissioning by March 2027; first product (400 TMT, mostly diesel) by end July 2026; MS plant starts Q3 FY27; full 9 MMT stabilized by March 2028

The mother unit CDU, VDU and DSDT per se and part of the Sulphur recovery unit to produce MS will be ready by end July. So, Bhaskarji, we are looking at about what - 400 TMT production after that?

items.statement: Upstream capex rollover ~10,000 crore per year for 3 years; target 100 wells/year onshore plus shallow water offshore wells
items.quote: As far as Capex is concerned, we are looking at a rollover Capex of 10,000 crores last year, this year and year after. That's about 100 wells per year in onshore basis. And this shallow water wells that we are drilling in offshore waters.

items.statement: Oil production target 4 MMT if 100 wells drilled; gas production target 3.35 BCM FY27, 5 BCM by FY28 (18 months after Duliajan feeder line and DNPL commissioning)
items.quote: And as far as Oil India is concerned you are right, the expectation or if I repeat it if we are able to drill 100 wells, we will touch 4 MMT. And gas, we will look at 3.35, 3.35 BCM. But 18 months down the line. This week and the week before every day we are getting new gains and new gains, having done 307, the number was what – 10,670 barrels per day, sorry, tons. As we speak today, it is 82,200 barrels. As we speak today, another highest 82,222 barrels per day.

items.statement: Gas production currently 8 MMSCMD; target 13-15 MMSCMD with pipeline evacuation; 15-18 deep/dry gas wells identified for ramp-up
items.quote: Oil India Limited today is sitting with a gas pool 2P reserve 121 MMT oil and oil equivalent. We can ramp up our production from 8 million to 13 million to 15 million standard cubic meter per day. We have already identified 15 to 18 deep wells and dry gas wells to be aligned to the authorized pipeline once it gets commissioned.

items.statement: DNPL mechanical completion done (2.5 MMSCMD); awaiting 7-day NRL shutdown for commissioning; DNPL to remain captive pipeline for Oil India molecules
items.quote: DNPL mechanical completion of 2.5 million standard cubic meter per day capacity is already done. Because of the Middle East crisis, NRL we are unable to take a shutdown of 7 days. Once we take a shutdown of 7 days DNPL will get commissioned and we will start pushing natural gas through DNPL. So, as we speak it is a captive pipeline.

items.statement: Duliajan feeder line authorization received; will enable evacuation to mainland India after NE CGD saturation
items.quote: We were waiting for this Duliajan feeder line authorization and this connectivity will actually open up the vista. Oil India Limited today is sitting with a gas pool 2P reserve 121 MMT oil and oil equivalent. We can ramp up our production from 8 million to 13 million to 15 million standard cubic meter per day.

items.quote: I am very glad to share that during the recent notification government has allocated 1.5 million standard cubic meter per day as New well gas allocation to Numaligarh Refinery. Now this New well Gas is primarily, now all of you know Oil India produces from the mature fields. So, these are all model revenue sharing contract. We do not foresee any change in the royalty per se. items.statement: Oilfields Act amended 2025; Stratigraphic Well Initiative and Samudra Manthan Mission launched to unlock 1M sq km for exploration; OALP Bid Round IX awarded 9 deepwater blocks to Oil India
items.quote: Due to the reforms by the Government of India from 2022-2023 onwards, 1 million square kilometers of area has been unlocked for exploration. So, for the first time under OALP Bid Round-IX, we got opportunities to submit bids for deep-water and ultra-deep-water blocks. And I can share with you, as Oil India Limited, we submitted 9 bids and were successful in securing all 9 blocks for exploration.

items.statement: TotalEnergies collaboration: service agreement for offshore exploration support; Total may invest if material drilling proposition arises; secures capital prudence
items.quote: Now the granularity is it is a service agreement where the experts or the domain experts of Total Energy is supporting Oil India Limited and should there be any material proposition to undertake drilling, Total will also have a say in terms of possible investments. So, this way we actually we have secured our capital prudence for our exploration efforts.

items.statement: India refined product consumption growing 7-8%; NRL 9 MMT output to serve NE and mainland via Siliguri tankage (Bihar, Odisha, East UP); Indo-Bangladesh pipeline continues
items.quote: India, as we know, is currently growing and the consumption of the refined products is growing at 7 to 8%. So, the 9 MMT production from NRL will find its market both in Northeast and also in mainland India, for which the Numaligarh-Siliguri Pipeline has been upgraded to 5.5 MMT per annum.

items.statement: NRL excise duty benefit ~3,000 crore FY26; no sunset clause after 9 MMT expansion; benefit calibrated to HSD FOB price; current margins equivalent to excise benefit
items.quote: Now, for this current year the amount that is accrued is about 3000 crores. But the one thing which I would like to share that the Numaligarh Refinery which is currently operating at 3 MMT, going forward will operate at 9 MMT, does not have any sunset clause for excise duty benefit. So, NRL will continue to get 50% north east excise duty benefit irrespective of the capacity expansion.

items.statement: Middle East crisis delayed NRL shutdown for DNPL hook-up; crisis response: fast-tracked Andaman appraisal seismic, monetized Bakhritibba DSF 12 months early, added 40 TPD LPG at NRL and 10 MMT crude
items.quote: We had to do appraisal of the gas find in the second well of Andaman Nicobar. In a normal case, one would wait, do tendering, bring another vessel and the appraisal process would have happened 1-year or 2-year down the line. We renegotiated the contract and got the seismic vessel to mobilize the spread on an ASAP basis and carry out the seismic data acquisition for our appraisal process.

items.statement: Released drillable location inventory increased from ~45 to 218; average well depth increased from 2,300-2,500m to 4,300m; 100 wells/year target sustained by two-tier scrutiny mechanism
items.quote: Today, as we speak, we carry a released drillable location inventory... Saloma, 218? It's 218. And we have our internal mechanism, a two-tier scrutiny mechanism to release these locations. So, to our mind, the Assam shelf, while we were doing an average depth of 2,300 to 2,500 meters three years ago, last year we did an average depth of 4,300 meters.

items.statement: Indo-Bangladesh Friendship Pipeline exporting HSD continues despite Bangladesh turmoil; not sole pivot for 9 MMT viability
items.quote: First is export option of NRL continues to stay unabated and despite the tumultuous turmoil that we witnessed in our neighboring country, we continue to export, that's HSD. That Indo-Bangladesh Friendship Pipeline continues to be one of our options to export.

items.statement: Continuous capability building: geologists, drilling engineers, geophysicists trained via ONGC and service provider facilities; deepwater field development capability to be added post-discovery
items.quote: We have sent our team both geologists, drilling engineers, geophysicists. All of them are on a continuous training program. And our drilling force is as we speak has been trained using ONGC's facility and with other service providers' facility. So that's a continuous process which is going on as part of capability building is concerned.

items.statement: Arunachal Pradesh gas evacuation pipeline nearing completion; two gas gathering stations at Nadua and Khagorijan; Baghjan, Kumchai, Chandmari, Mechaki, Kharsang fields identified for gas ramp-up; 11 compressor stations operational, 11 more
items.quote: We have built a pipeline to evacuate natural gas from Arunachal Pradesh to Duliajan. That's nearing completion. Any day, we will commission and announce it. We are building two gas gathering stations, one is at Nadua, one is at Khagorijan. The Baghjan field is sitting on a huge gas pool, Arunachal Pradesh's Kumchai field is sitting on a huge gas field.

items.quote: We plan to get down to at least below 220 days to 210 days.
