items.quote: What happens with Quick Comm is that your logistics cost, the forward courier charges and the return courier charges go down drastically. And that helps any brand to improve their gross margins.

items.statement: TRIBE and Fitness Exchange to drive margin improvement and premiumization
items.quote: the brand where we are looking to expand our margins a little, Forcas Studios Limited (FORCAS) H2 & FY26 Post Earnings Conference Call May 25, 2026 12:00 PM IST both through men and women. Also, taking TRIBE to e-comm and Quick Comm now, we'll see a higher ASP, again, because our overheads and the basic infrastructure is set. So over there, the premiumization will help

items.statement: FY26 revenue grew 39% YoY to Rs. 198 crores; PAT grew 58% to Rs. 13.6 crores
items.quote: I am pleased to share that during FY26, our revenue from operations grew to approximately Rs. 198 crores, reflecting a strong growth of nearly 39% year-on-year. More importantly, this growth was accompanied by significant profitability expansion. Our profit after tax increased by nearly 58% year-on-year to approximately Rs. 13.6 crores

items.statement: H2FY26 revenue Rs. 114 crores, PAT nearly Rs. 8 crores
items.quote: H2FY26 was particularly strong for us, where we delivered revenue of approximately Rs. 114 crores with PAT of nearly Rs. 8 crores, reflecting strong momentum across channels and brands.

items.statement: Online repeat customer rate 29-30%; offline retailer repeat rate 65-70% within 4-6 months
items.quote: But the gross data which we have is around 29% - 30%. So, that is on the online. For offline, almost 65% - 70% of our retailers repeat our products within 4-6 months.

items.statement: Cash conversion cycle increased from 168 to 251 days in FY26; expects improvement in couple of years as brands mature
items.quote: I believe gradually when our higher margin products are also set in the market, this cash flow will improve in a couple of years for sure.

items.statement: Talent acquisition and brandification process identified as key bottlenecks for growth
items.quote: I believe, honestly, there are two challenges which we need to solve. Number one, yes, talent is one thing which we need to focus more on and need to hire more people from the industry and established brands. And number two is the brandification process, it doesn't have a particular way of doing.

items.statement: Advertising spend at 3-4% of revenue on marketplaces; will start offline brand spend in FY27
items.quote: Our FY26 numbers, exact numbers is not handy of the percentage of advertisement spent on marketplaces. But the ballpark figure we take as a company is between 3% to 4%.

items.statement: Quick Comm revenue Rs. 7.5 crores in FY26
items.quote: So, our Quick Comm revenue this year was around Rs. 7.5 cr.

items.statement: Brandification learning curve and talent hiring are key execution risks
items.quote: And number two is the brandification process, it doesn't have a particular way of doing. They don't have a same copybook strategy which you can follow and brandify yourself. So, this is a learning curve where you need to learn, implement, fail, learn, implement, fail and find your own way.

items.statement: Offline distribution expanding from 8 to 10 states in FY27
items.quote: So offline, we are present into eight states and we'll be adding two states this year.

items.statement: Myntra collaboration partnerships in talks as growth lever
items.quote: In Myntra, we are also in talks with some collaborated partnerships with Myntra brands. So that is also one lever of growth, which we will take.

items.statement: Target 3,000-3,500 keys and 50 hotels by FY28
items.quote: The target of 3000 to 3,500 k eys by 2028 March and having 50 hotels is the target what Grand Continent is looking at

items.statement: Aim to reach 72-73% occupancy target
items.quote: We have increased from 61 to 68% and every day we are looking at increasing it and we are putting in all our efforts to ensure that we reach the target of roundabout 72 to 73%.

items.statement: Expect to recover GST-hit margins within next two years
items.quote: Next two years, we are sure that we, next year itself, you can see a very big change into it in next one or two years, I'm sure we'll work on this.

items.statement: Aim to maintain FY26 occupancy growth rate in FY27 and FY28
items.quote: When you see what was added in FY 25, you are what you are seeing it in FY 26, the same percentage we will try to maintain it in FY 27 and 28.

items.statement: Funding next 600-700 keys via sanctioned bank limits and internal accruals; no equity dilution planned now
items.quote: we have got already a sanction limit from the bank right now. And we also will have good internal accruals inside. So I'm sure that, you know, we will be able to save through for th e next 600 to 700 keys

items.statement: May raise additional debt in FY28 for remaining keys; no equity dilution
items.quote: Going forward for the next year, 2027-28 financial year, 2028 financial years, yes, we might require some funds, but based on the number of hotels we are going to sign up and based on the internal accruals what we are going to have for this current year, based on that, we will plan and raise o nly debt

items.statement: Pipeline of signings across Varanasi, Ayodhya, Somnath, Jaipur, Chennai ECR, Gurgaon, Bangalore, Rameshwaram expected to go live in 2026-27
items.quote: We have built a very strong pipeline with signings across Varanasi, Ayodhya, Somnath, Jaipur, Chennai ECR, one more in Gurgaon, Bangalore, and Rameshwaram, most of which are expected to go live in the year 2026 -27.

items.statement: ~8 hotels opening in next 4-5 months; another 7-8 by 2028
items.quote: We have round about 8 hotels coming up in the next four, five months, which we are planning to open one after the other. And by 2028, we are planning with another 7, 8 hotels.

items.statement: Mature business hotels delivered EBITDA margins exceeding 28%
items.quote: Importantly, our mature business hotels delivered EBITDA margins exceeding 28%, reinforcing the strength of our operating and profit and portfo lio mix

items.statement: Lease rental cost rose to 30-31% of revenue due to GST impact; target to bring back to 26-27%
items.quote: Now it is gone up to around about 30 to 31 percent. Yes, that's it. That's the thing. So how can we can bring it back to 27, 26 percent?

items.statement: Target historical 30% EBITDA margin in next 1-2 years before 2028
items.quote: I cannot guarantee or assure you of 30%, but we will be trying to get into those numbers as best, as close as possible.

items.statement: Revising room rentals up 8-10% to offset GST impact
items.quote: We have started revising our room rentals by 8 to 10 percent. We have already started increasing it, which we are going to increase it a little bit more demanding based on the demand of the property.

items.statement: Exploring revenue-share and management models to avoid 18% GST on lease rentals
items.quote: We are in discussion with the new hotel owners, whether we can go in for a revenue share rather than going in for a lease model, which can avoid this 18% of the GST. And third thing, Grand Continent is also loo king out to expand not only on a lease model, but also into a management model

items.statement: Strong domestic travel demand, rising spiritual tourism, increasing branded hotel penetration in tier 2/3 cities
items.quote: Looking ahead, the hospitality outlook remains highly positive, driven by strong domestic travel demand raising spiritual tourism and increasing presentation, sorry, increasing penetration of branded hotels across tier 2 and tier 3 cities.

items.statement: Target portfolio mix: 60-65% corporate, 20-25% pilgrimage, 10% leisure hotels
items.quote: As I have already told before, it will be 60 to 65% of our group hotels will be a corporate hotel, 20 to 25% will be going to be a pilgrimage centre and 10, 10% would be a leisure destinations.

items.statement: Expanded sales team from 6-7 to 16-17 people; opened regional offices in Ahmedabad, Delhi, Bombay, expanding to Bangalore, Chennai, Hyderabad
items.quote: Today, from a strength of six to seven people on a sales team, today we have headed by a very senior gentleman by name Ankit Upreti, who has taken over as the head of sales India. And we have right now 16 to 17 people in this entire sales force in India.

items.statement: India occupancy 68%, ARR ~Rs 3,960 in FY26 vs 61% occupancy and Rs 3,750 ARR in FY25
items.quote: Operationally, India business continued to perform well with occupancy at 68% and an average room rent of rupees 3,960. Our mature, our mature business hotels remains the primary drivers of profitability, while leisure and new properties are stabilising in line with expectations.

items.statement: US portfolio: 3 hotels, 367 keys under Holiday Inn, Comfort Suites, Ramada; profitable in short tenure
items.quote: Our entry into the premier and luxury segment, which was our 25th property, was with Udaipur, marked an important milest one for Grand Continent Hotels Limited. Our defining highlight of FY 2026 has been our international expansion. We, we started our operations, our first operations in US portfolio for lease-led model with three hotels and 367 keys under the globally recogn ised brands such as Ho

items.statement: Consolidated FY26 revenue Rs 140.54 crore (+94% YoY), Adjusted EBITDA Rs 27.96 crore, PAT Rs 1.41 crore (operational PAT Rs 17.5-18 crore before Rs 5.4 crore GST impact)
items.value: Rs 140.54 cr revenue, Rs 27.96 cr EBITDA, Rs 1.41 cr PAT
items.quote: For the entire year of 2026, revenue stood at 140.54 crore, up by 94% over FY 2025. Adjusted EBITDA was 27.96 crore and PAT stood at 1.41 crore, while India margins are temporary impact due to GST input credit changes in September 2025.

items.statement: H2 FY26 revenue Rs 84.83 crore (+108% YoY), Adjusted EBITDA Rs 21.48 crore (+136% YoY), PAT Rs 10.10 crore (+129% YoY)
items.value: Rs 84.83 cr revenue, Rs 21.48 cr EBITDA, Rs 10.10 cr PAT
items.quote: Coming to the financial performance in H2FY 2026, has been one of our strongest periods in our history. The revenue stood at 84.83 crore, up by 108% year on year, with 52% subsequently. Adjusted EBITDA was around 21.48 crore, up by 136% year on year. Profit after tax grew 129% year on year to 10.10 crore.

items.statement: GST rate cut from 12% to 5% on room tariff removed input credit on 18% GST paid on lease rentals, causing ~Rs 5.4 crore PAT impact
items.quote: Now the GST is revived to 5% and that 5%, we are not able to take the input tax. So because of it, your output tax and the rental still remains at 18%, but what we collect from our customers is 5%, which we are not which we are not able to match it across.

items.statement: Mitigating GST impact via specified premises for F&B input credit, already showing impact in April-May
items.quote: we have taken certain measures within the purview of the law, like we have gone in for specified pre mises of some of our properties, majority of our properties, wherein we can take the input credit on our F&B business as well as proportionately on the other input credits available. And this has already started showing some impact in the month of April and May

items.statement: Current ratio stable; will improve as new hotels yield profits
items.quote: On the balance sheet numbers, it's clearly visible that whatever funds raised through the IPO or through the bank has been invested in the operations and therefore the Cap ex, our fixed assets has grown in the balance sheet to from 62 crores to 83 crores with the investment in the new hotels and the current ratio almost remains the same. It will improve once the many of the new hotels start yieldi

items.statement: Strengthened leadership across operations, finance, procurement, compliance, HR; added independent directors
items.quote: We also made significant progress in strengthening our organisational capacities with enhanced leadership across operations, finance, procurement, compliance, and human resources, ensuring we are very, very well prepared for the next phase of growth.

items.statement: Dubai franchise under review; may exit if no improvement by June due to Gulf situation
items.quote: Yes, Dubai has got a hit right now because of the situation in the Gulf. Yet the right now the franchisee is still going on with them, but we are in discussion with the landowners on continuing with that. But if we foresee no i mprovements in this by this month end or by the beginning of June, then we may have to reverse out of

items.statement: US expansion paused at 3 hotels; will evaluate after one season before further growth
items.quote: We are not going to increase the number of hotels as such. We have just taken these three properties, we are analysing it, we are studying it. We wanted to at least have one season of it, one H1 going through, seeing the profitability and seeing how far we can, how far we can stabilise it and then based on those results, we are going to increase it.

items.statement: Mature hotels expected to maintain 27-30% EBITDA margin; new hotels will not materially drag consolidated margins as mature portfolio grows to 75-80% of keys.
items.quote: So the mature hotels, once it stabilizes, we are sure that we should stick on to an EBITDA of what we are delivering right now. Anywhere between 27 to 30% is a good number for us to get it done.

items.statement: US hotels expected to reach 60-65% occupancy in FY27.
items.quote: Sir, if we can, we can anywhere look anywhere between 65, 60 to 65%, Sir. 65% year to date.

items.statement: Revenue-share model (25-30% of top line) under evaluation to offset 18% GST impact; not yet signed, legal and auditor review ongoing.
items.quote: So instead of giving them a fixed lease rental, if I could give them a 25 to 30% on the top line and everything else, we take it back. So that will exclude and benefit of GST for us, that will have a bigger benefit for us.

items.statement: Pre-opening cost per key currently 7-8 lakhs, target 7-7.5 lakhs; lease rental capped at 27-28% of revenue.
items.quote: We have always stayed in the budget of somewhere around about 6 to 7 lakhs per room key. That will be the pre-opening cost for us. Though the cost has shot up high and, you know, things have gone up very high on the cost part of it. There is an increase, 6 to 7 lakhs is what our target was. Now it is lingering around between 7 to 8 lakhs.

items.statement: April occupancy dipped 4-5% vs prior month, but April FY26 revenue and occupancy up ~25-30% vs April FY25; May-June inquiries strong.
items.quote: When I compare ourselves with FY25 April and FY26 April, We have almost done around about 30% more than what we have done in FY26, FY in the year 25 April and 26 April. There has been an increase of 25% on the entire revenue and the occupancy.

items.statement: Work-from-home has minor impact; some guests book long stays (15-20 days) to work from hotels.
items.quote: Work from home, yes, it has been there. But a lot of people, I would say that, you know, they in Bangalore, they are working from our hotels also. They come, they take a long-term room from us for 15-20 days and they work from here also.

items.statement: 600 keys signed via MOUs for FY27; advances paid to landowners; 500-600 keys targeted for FY28 after detailed feasibility studies.
items.quote: As of now, we have signed the MOUs. We already signed and paid some advances to all the landowners. We are having approximately 600 keys which have, we have signed for this year.

items.statement: US investment: $1.8M total, of which $1.3M refundable security deposit; per-key cost ~$6k vs ~$7k in India.
items.quote: As far as your CapEx is concerned, we just had, you know, a total investment of 1.8 million there, US dollars, out of which 1.3 million USD is a refundable security deposit.

items.statement: Average collection period 25-30 days across portfolio.
items.quote: The average collection period would be around 25 to 30 days on an average. Am I audible? Yeah, as I mentioned, the average collection figure overall, all the company total put together would be around 25 to 30 days of credit.

items.statement: Refundable security deposits (non-current assets) ~Rs 52 crore on balance sheet; FY26 cash outflow Rs 32.5 crore mainly for new deposits.
items.quote: Majorly that way, if you see the schedule in the balance sheets, non-current assets, it represents that only, security deposits.

items.statement: GST input credit loss a significant hit; exploring revenue-share model (25-30% of revenue) to mitigate; legal and auditor review underway.
items.quote: We are trying to work on it, but we are expecting a better clarity on it from our legal heads and from the auditors. Once we get into it, then we will start looking into it.

items.statement: Dubai franchise severely impacted by geopolitics; no tourists, only locals; decision on continuation by month-end; MOU for 122-room Deira property mutually cancelled.
items.quote: Now we don't have any tourists coming down there at this point of a time. And only the locals are travelling there and we have given some type of an accommodation for the locals where they can stay in the weekends and spend their time with their families. And now we are in discussion with the landowners, whether we continue with them as being a franchisor or whether we have to discontinue it. Yes,

items.statement: Pan-India corporate tie-ups rolling out; rates negotiated annually; no fixed room-night commitments but volume-driven; audit and security verification required before onboarding.
items.quote: So when we tie up, we give a rate to them for all the places and depending upon the locations, we give them a different rates and different ARRs. So we put them across in a record and give it to them and we also talk to them about the upcoming properties which w e are going to open for this financial year

items.statement: Portfolio shifting to 75-80% mature hotels (28 hotels) vs 20-25% new (8-9 hotels) in FY27, supporting margin stability.
items.quote: today we are sitting at a matured hotels or close to 30 hotels which are almost matured. I don't say 30. 28, because Rameshwaram and Gurgaon are just started now. 28 hotels are almost getting into the mature segment, and we are going to have only 8 -9 hotels coming up for this year.

items.statement: Targeting 5-10% ARR increase in spiritual segment (currently ~Rs 4,000) to improve margins.
items.quote: And then we also ensure that we have a good bottom line average room rent of round about 4000 to now we are trying to scale it up by another 5- 10% this year so that, you know, the margins will be much stronger.

items.statement: Occupancy target for mature portfolio: 70-72% year-to-date.
items.quote: As far as their occupancies and other things are concerned, we concentrate on the ensuring that we have a year-to-date occupancy we maintain at 70-72%.

items.statement: Loyalty programme in final stages; launch expected in next couple of months.
items.quote: We are in the final stages of getting that closed. Mostly in the next couple of months, we'll be rolling out our loyalty programs.

items.statement: No new international expansion beyond US; Europe not being explored; focus entirely on India 3,000 keys in 24 months.
items.quote: No, right now, no. Our main concentration and only concentration is going to be only in India. We are going to develop hotels in India. We are not looking at any other destinations as of now.

items.statement: Effective tax rate currently 25%; future rate depends on statute changes.
items.quote: That would depend on the statute as of now, it's 25%. It will depend on the statute in the coming income tax laws.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth target of around 60% year-on-year
items.quote: And just coming year also we are looking out for growth around 60 % from last year.

items.statement: FY27 PAT margin guidance of 4% to 4.5% excluding gold price appreciation
items.quote: I would talk about PAT margin, around 4%, 4.5%.

items.statement: FY27 EBITDA margin guidance of 7% to 8%
items.quote: EBITDA would be around 7% to 8%.

items.statement: Long-term target of INR4,000-5,000 crores revenue by 2030
items.quote: So, yes, yes, we have a lot of, we look around INR4,000 crores to INR5,000 crores business around 2030.

items.statement: Planned capex of around INR50 crores for FY27
items.quote: Yes, around INR50 crores.

items.statement: Current manufacturing capacity of 2,500 kg per year with 65% utilization
items.quote: Current capacity is around 2,500 kilos.

items.statement: Capacity expansion planned to 6-7 tons per year with new building of 20,000-25,000 sq ft
items.quote: And we are planning to expand and make it, means we are planning to acquire more buildings and all around where our capacity would go around 6 to 7 tons a year.

items.statement: Utilization expected to improve to 70-75% in FY27 from current 65%
items.quote: But overall, yes, this year we will have around 70% to 75% of utilization.

items.statement: Onboarded 112 new clients in FY26, expanding retailer network across India
items.quote: This momentum helped us onboard 112 new clients during FY26, sig nificantly expanding our retailer network and strengthening our market

items.statement: Diamond jewelry currently 2% of revenue, targeting over INR200 crores annually in 2 years
items.quote: So, diamond jewellery we have just recently started. It's like around 2% and all. And like in couple of years, we should be reaching around more than INR200 crores.

items.statement: Entered plain gold jewelry segment recently, adding to CZ, natural diamond and lab-grown diamond portfolio
items.quote: And now we recently stepped into plain gold jewelry also. So, we have a lot of demand in plain gold jewelry also.

items.statement: UAE subsidiary approved; exports expected to jump to 10-20% of revenue from current 1%
items.quote: So, once if UAE subsidiary starts, so its export sales will jump up to 10% to 20% immediately.

items.statement: Targeting GCC countries, Singapore, Malaysia, Australia through distributors and exhibitions
items.quote: So, as, like, we have started participating in foreign exhibitions and all. So, as I said in earlier thing, like, we are trying customers in Singapore, Malaysia, and Australia and all.

items.statement: H2 FY26 EBITDA margin 8.10% (+187 bps YoY), PAT margin 5.1% (+123 bps YoY)
items.quote: EBITDA margin improved by 187 basis points to 8.10 %, while PAT margin expanded by 123 basis points to 5.1%.

items.statement: Plain gold jewelry addition lowers blended PAT margin to 4-4.5% from previous 4.5-5% target
items.quote: Yes, it's because of the plain gold jewelry what we have added. So, that's how we'll be -- our margin will go down around -- it's going to be operational margin I'm talking about, which will be around 4% to 4.5%.

items.statement: Healthy demand driven by festive/wedding seasons, repeat business, and deeper market penetration
items.quote: During the year, we witnessed healthy demand driven by festive and wedding seasons, sales repeat business from existing customers, and deeper penetration across both existing and new markets.

items.statement: Gold price volatility has not affected jewelry demand; demand remains strong across India
items.quote: Gold prices were high last quarter also, and last to last quarter also. So, demand is there all over India. So, it has not affected our business in terms of gold prices.

items.statement: Working capital cycle of 45-60 days; negative operating cash flow due to gold inventory stocking
items.quote: 45 to 60 days is our working capital cycle.

items.statement: Planning to raise INR50 crores via bank borrowing for FY27 growth; debt-equity to remain below 1x
items.quote: Yes. Around INR50 crores we are taking additional funds.

items.statement: Top 10 customers contribute ~50% revenue; diversifying via 112 new clients in FY26 and international expansion
items.quote: As I said, we have new 112 firms and we are expanding our business across India as well as abroad.

items.statement: Design innovation (400-500 new designs/month) is key USP driving growth and client acquisition
items.quote: So, we have around 400-500 designs every month, which is our main USP. So, that's how we've been able to grow up year -on-year.

items.statement: PM's recent statement on gold expected to impact gold bars/coins, not jewelry demand
items.quote: No, I think that would be more on gold bar than gold coins and all. I think jewelry is not going to be the concern.

items.statement: Negative operating cash flow structural due to gold inventory model; no immediate improvement expected
items.quote: In this business, cash flow positive means basically whatever the money comes, we buy gold and we manufacture and we keep the stock ready. That is why it is a negative cash flow what is seen.

items.statement: FY27 store opening target of 500-700 stores
items.quote: we are quite confident that in the current financial year, FY27, we will open somewhere between 500 to 700 stores.

items.statement: Moderating store expansion pace in Q2 and Q3 FY27 to improve profitability
items.quote: we plan to slow down the expansion during Q2 and Q3, possibly for one or two quarters. This calibrated approach is aimed at improving profitability.

items.statement: Long-term target of 5,000+ Davaindia stores by FY29
items.quote: we remain confident in our long-term vision of scaling to 5,000+ Davaindia stores by FY29

items.statement: FY26 capex of INR 114 crores primarily for planned store expansion
items.quote: The increase in inventory and capex is primarily in advance of the planned store expansion.

items.statement: Added 997 Davaindia stores in FY26 (804 COCO, 193 FOFO), total network 2,579 stores
items.quote: During the year, we added 997 new Davaindia stores including 804 COCO stores and 193 FOFO stores, which we believe is the highest ever addition in the pharmaceutical retail segment in a single financial year.

items.statement: Added 248 stores in Q4 FY26 (218 COCO, 30 FOFO)
items.quote: From a Davaindia operation standpoint, we added 248 stores in Q4 alone, including 218 COCO and 30 FOFO stores.

items.statement: Expect ~200+ store openings in Q1 FY27 from remaining pipeline
items.quote: From the remaining pipeline, we expect to open roughly 200+ stores in the current quarter.

items.statement: FY27 store additions: ~500+ COCO and ~100-150 FOFO stores
items.quote: Out of the total ~700 stores planned, approximately ~100 to 150 stores may be opened under the FOFO model, while the remaining ~500+ stores will be COCO.

items.statement: FY26 same-store growth >40% for 852 stores operational as of March 2025
items.quote: During FY26, all our 852 stores operational as on March '25 have delivery and overall SSG of more than 40% during this financial year.

items.statement: Mature stores (24+ months) SSG 35-40%, younger stores (12-24 months) SSG 55-60% in FY26
items.quote: store age 24 plus months have recorded SSG of 35% to 40%, while store age between 12 to 24 months have achieved even stronger SSG of 55% to 60% in this financial year.

items.statement: 234 stores (pre-FY24) delivered ~24% YoY SSG in FY26 (GST-adjusted)
items.quote: For example, we had 234 stores as of 31 st March 2024, if I compare their revenue as on Q4 FY25 versus Q4 FY26 for this particular cohort, the growth is over 24% on an adjusted basis, factoring in the GST

items.statement: 29 stores (54+ months) annualized SSG ~17% YoY (GST-adjusted)
items.quote: Yes, for that specific cohort, the annualized SSG growth is about 17% on a year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Average wallet spend for 2-3 year old stores: INR 270-290
items.quote: Yes, for stores that are more than two to three years old, the average wallet spend is in the range of approximately INR 270 to INR 290.

items.statement: FY26 consolidated gross margin expanded 714 bps to 60.28%
items.quote: Gross margin expanded significantly by 714 basis points to 60.28%, supported by scale benefit and improved product mix.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA turned positive at INR 2,597 lakhs (4.82% margin) vs negative in FY25
items.quote: FY26 marked a turnaround at the operating level as we achieved a positive EBITDA, which stood at INR 2,597 lakhs compared to negative EBITDA in FY25. EBITDA margin improved to 4.82% for the full year.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 EBITDA INR 1,191 lakhs at 7.3% margin
items.quote: On quarterly basis as well, performance has shown meaningful improvement. EBITDA stood to INR 1,191 lakhs with margin of 7.3%, reflecting both sequential and Y-o-Y improvement.

items.statement: COCO store gross margins >70%, sustainable and improving
items.quote: COCO store's gross margins are over 70%. While, for communication purposes including in our presentation we typically indicate around ~60%, the actual margins are materially higher, closer to 70%+ at the COCO level.

items.statement: Marketing spend FY26: INR 18 crores vs INR 10.5 crores in FY25, proportional to sales growth
items.quote: in the last financial year, we incurred approximately INR 18 crores purely towards advertising. In comparison, in the previous year, the spend was around INR 10.5 crores.

items.statement: FOFO model margin 40-55%, COCO model margin 10-15% on billing
items.quote: In the FOFO model, we sell directly and add our margin. Typically, the margin in FOFO ranges between 40% to 55%. In the COCO model, we operate at a lower margin, where we add roughly 10% to 15% while billing.

items.statement: Payable days reduced due to MSME compliance (45-day payment rule), 70% procurement from MSMEs
items.quote: The improvement is mainly due to MSME-related compliance. As per regulations, payments to MSME suppliers need to be made within 45 days. Since a significant portion around 70% of our procurement is from MSMEs, this has led to a reduction in payable days.

items.statement: Completed INR 350 crores QIP to strengthen balance sheet
items.quote: We have successfully completed a INR 350 crores QIP, significantly strengthening our balance sheet and providing capital to support our expansion journey.

items.statement: Increased stake in Everyday Herbal Beauty Care to 87.78% for backward integration
items.quote: We increased our stake in Everyday Herbal Beauty Care Limited to 87.78%, reinforcing our backward integration strategy and enhancing control over our consumer product portfolio.

items.statement: Annual footfalls doubled YoY to 182+ lakhs in FY26
items.quote: We also witnessed a substantial increase in customer engagement with annual footfalls rising to over 182 lakhs customers, nearly doubling year-on-year

items.statement: Davaindia 100% private label portfolio driving margin expansion
items.quote: This improvement is largely driven by Davaindia's operating model, which is built on a 100% private label portfolio along with an integrated manufacturing-to-retail approach.

items.statement: GMV reached INR 45,706 lakhs in FY26 for Davaindia
items.quote: GMV reaching INR 45,706 lakhs, demonstrating strong traction at the store level and improving our unit economics as the network mature.

items.statement: Store maturation 3-5 years to reach steady-state INR 6-7 lakhs monthly sales
items.quote: Based on the current data trends, we believe store maturation typically falls within a 3-to-5-year range. Within this period, stores can achieve a steady-state monthly sales level of around INR 6 lakhs to INR 7 lakhs.

items.statement: No store closures in last year; <1-1.5% closure rate for 2+ year stores over 1-2 years
items.quote: in the last one year, we have not closed even a single COCO store. If I specifically talk about stores that are more than two years old which is roughly around 234 stores there could potentially be a very small number of underperforming stores. However, even in that case, the closure rate would be extremely low, within the range of about 1% to 1.5%.

items.statement: FY27 EBITDA margin guidance of 9-9.5%
items.quote: Whole year. For FY27, guidance is what we are trying to achieve 9-9.5%.

items.statement: Management expects ~18% revenue CAGR and ~200 bps margin expansion over the next three years if economic conditions remain stable, but may modify or defer plans due to geopolitical developments.
items.quote: We assume that considering the next three-year plan with the CapEx, around 18% of revenue CAGR growth, 200 approx. BPS margin expansion, ROCE improvement between 18 to 20%, the forgoing assumption are considered achievable provided that the prevailing economic condition remains stable.

items.statement: Management hopes to cross the Rs 1,000 crore revenue milestone in FY27 if demand improves in the next month or two, while maintaining margins at current levels.
items.quote: So, but what we expect that at least if things improve in the next, in the next month or two months, then definitely in the second-half, we'll see the growth that we anticipate to you know, cross the thousand crore benchmark and milestone hopefully in this financial year.

items.statement: Malaysian mine operational; plant construction minimum 12 months, commissioning expected early next financial year.
items.quote: For the Malaysian operation, the mines have already been, you know started operating and currently we are in that scenario of you know, organizing the mine in a proper way and followed with the construction of the plant, which will be a minimum of, you know, 12 months.

items.statement: Sievert JV phase 1 established, phase 2 going live in next few months; meaningful consolidated contribution expected by end of current financial year.
items.quote: The Sievert operations which is a new operation which has already been established in its first phase in the past few months. The second phase will go live probably in the next few months. And overall, if you look at this JV, the real outcome would be you can see it possibly by the end of the financial year.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin stable at ~12%; full-year FY26 EBITDA margin 12.9% supported by better product mix.
items.quote: EBITDA margin remains stable about 12% reflecting the pricing discipline, whereas the EBITDA grew at 9.6% YoY to 31.8 crore

items.statement: Management targets ROCE of 18-20% by FY30 if CapEx projects are delivered on time.
items.quote: We assume that considering the next three-year plan with the CapEx, around 18% of revenue CAGR growth, 200 approx. BPS margin expansion, ROCE improvement between 18 to 20%.

items.statement: Demand recovery observed from January 2026 across paints, polymers, rubber; Q4 FY26 revenue grew 14.8% YoY and 21.5% QoQ.
items.quote: Basically since January of 2026, we saw an upward trend in terms of the demand coming back in variety of industries that we are catering to and post that In February also we saw a stable uptrend in terms of the demand.

items.statement: Near-term demand expected to remain volatile; growth drivers for FY27 include plastics, rubber, inks and construction chemicals outside paints.
items.quote: But when we look at an industry specific case scenario, then I think apart from paints, if you're looking at then plastics and rubber and you know inks and construction chemicals is something that we are quite robust on for this financial year and the coming years as well.

items.statement: Paint segment contribution ~46% of revenue, flat YoY; exports stable at 14%; specialty/higher value-added products increasing.
items.quote: The revenue pie indicates the paint contribution above 46% of the revenue indicating A gradual shift to polymer and rubber segments, showing a better transition compared to the previous. Exports contribution are stable at 14%.

items.statement: Launched 35-40 new products annually; new products contribute ~4-5% of revenue; R&D focusing on nano-sized materials, construction chemicals, tyre additives, cosmetic applications.
items.quote: So about 4 to 5% is what the contribution usually comes in from the new products which are you know usually taking shape both from 20 microns and 20 microns Nano Windows Limited.

items.statement: ~30% of raw material requirement met from owned mines (mainly Malaysian); 70% sourced externally; some domestic mines under environmental clearance.
items.quote: So out of that, approximately about 30% of our total raw material requirement comes from the mines and 70% comes from external sources.

items.statement: Facing fuel/gas cost hikes and availability issues; managing via multiple sources; not currently affecting production but future government restrictions could change situation.
items.quote: We definitely are facing a lot of issues in terms of the gas or the fuels that we use currently. But our teams are efficient enough managing those tough situations with balanced approach in terms of the hikes and the fuels cost which are happening currently and the availability which is there by having multiple sources of available resources that are there with the team of ours.

items.statement: Cost increases (fuel, gas, forex, freight, raw materials) passed to customers on case-by-case basis with a lag of few days to weeks.
items.quote: But what we do is that we've discussed case by case basis with our customers and in many cases we do pass it on to our customers, but it doesn't happen immediately. It happens over a period of time.

items.statement: Inventory turnover improved from 5.8x to 8.3x; current ratio strengthened to 1.9x; net working capital utilization expected to remain at FY26 levels in FY27; no material payment delays currently.
items.quote: See we if you see our entire cash flow cycle that have been given in our balance sheets, there is no such gaps in our net working capital range. So to the extent of FY26 will remain the same in terms of net working capital utilization.

items.statement: Net debt/equity reduced to 0.1x in FY26 from 0.4x; free cash flow generated in FY26 was Rs 42.28 crore; aspiration to become debt-free long-term but no timeline given.
items.quote: The net equity ratio remained to 0.1 X from 0.4 X in FY26. Strong cash generation improves funding capability for the future CapEx as well as the lower leverage reduction reduce financial risk and finance cost burden.

items.statement: Malaysian CapEx funded 70% debt, 30% equity; domestic CapEx funded internally; no equity raise indicated.
items.quote: So largely for our domestic plans, the CapEx would be in form of the internal approvals, whereas for Malaysian entity, we are planning to have a ratio around 70 to 30, that is 30% debt.

items.statement: Doffner JV already contributing; Sievert JV phase 2 in next few months, meaningful contribution by FY end; Malaysian limestone mine operational, plant commissioning in ~12 months.
items.quote: So Doffner is already you know it is a different kind of a JV setup which we have already initiated and that is already contributing to the overall picture. The Sievert operations which is a new operation which has already been established in its first phase in the past few months.

items.statement: Customer off-take understandings updated regularly for few weeks/months ahead; no fixed long-term contracts; mutual understanding revised with demand changes.
items.quote: We have a mutual understanding with all our customers in terms of the off takes at the beginning of the year that they're anticipating and that keeps changing with the changing demands because of the macroeconomic environment changing.

items.statement: Market share ranges 10-30% depending on product; many international and domestic competitors, most unlisted; competitor list to be shared separately.
items.quote: So basically it's, it's the market share if we look at it, it ranges anywhere from 10% to 30% depending on what kind of things are talking about. So we can't generalise a product basically upon an overall picture.

items.statement: Food/pharma grade calcium carbonate requires new licensing and setup; not currently manufactured but potential future entry after market assessment.
items.quote: Yes, currently we don't possess any of the licensing for developing any food grade or pharma grade calcium carbonates in our company. But definitely in the future we anticipate to get into this kind of business once we understand this market well.

items.statement: Geopolitical uncertainties, prolonged monsoon impact, fuel/gas cost hikes, forex volatility, supply chain disruptions cited as key risks; CapEx plans may be modified or deferred.
items.quote: However, in light to the current geopolitical development, the Company shall modify or defer its phase plans accordingly.

items.statement: Revenue CAGR ~12% over FY22-26 (Rs 613 cr to Rs 954 cr); EBITDA CAGR ~12-13% (Rs 79 cr to Rs 123 cr); PAT CAGR ~14% (Rs 35 cr to Rs 67 cr).
items.value: 12% revenue CAGR, 12-13% EBITDA CAGR, 14% PAT CAGR
items.quote: In this industrial applications, the revenue increased from 613 crores in FY22 to 954 crores in FY26. This is a showcase that CAGR approximately grow about 12% over the five years. The EBITDA has increased from 79 crores to 123 crores over the five years with CAGR approx. of 12 to 13% despite multiple industry disruptions PAT almost double from 35 crores to 67 crores with the CAGR approx. of 14%.

items.statement: Automation and renewable energy (solar, hybrid, wind) initiatives planned over next 3 years to reduce power costs and improve capacity; part of CapEx plan.
items.quote: There are a lot of automation plans which are already you know in place. Many of our older processes which we were following traditionally in you know, our production facilities. With the CapEx that we are you know have incurred in the last two years and with the future CapEx that we are expecting in terms of the new age milling processes that we will be following which goes which takes care of a

items.statement: Board approved guarantees up to Rs 2.5 crore for a JV partner's borrowings; not for director-owned competing entities.
items.quote: This was this sorted approach from the board. Actually this is for our one of the JV partners that quantum was around 2 1/2 crores. OK.

items.statement: Targeting better than industry revenue growth in FY27 with EBITDA margins improving towards 8% as operating leverage returns and cost discipline takes effect
items.quote: For FY27, we are targeting better than industry revenue growth. We expect EBITDA margins to improve towards 8% as operating leverage returns, input cost pressures moderate and our cost discipline initiatives take effect.

items.statement: Expecting significant improvement in working capital intensity and operating and free cash flow generation in FY27
items.quote: Working capital intensity is expected to improve significantly as inventory and the receivable cycles improves. We expect to improve operating and free cash flow generation in FY27.

items.statement: Spent INR785 crores on capex in FY26, with INR500 crores on land and building, INR70 crores on washing machine plant and machinery, INR165 crores on RAC plant and machinery
items.quote: Out of the total INR785 crores that we have spent this year in the capex, almost close to INR500 crores has actually gone into the land and building piece.

items.statement: Planning capex of close to INR400 crores in FY27 and targeting 4x plus asset turn by 2029
items.quote: We will be probably be doing a capex of close to INR400 crores this year. We should be able to utilize these assets and get to an asset turn of 4x plus by 2029.

items.statement: New refrigerant manufacturing facility at Sri City planned for commercial production by Q4 FY27, meaningful revenue stream in FY28
items.quote: We are developing a new refrigerant manufacturing facility in Sri City in South India, which is progressing well. We plan to start commercial production by quarter 4 of FY27, and this will become a meaningful revenue stream in FY28.

items.statement: Rotary compressor manufacturing facility at Supa plant with machinery ordered, installation from August 2026, operations by Q4 FY27, 2 million capacity in phase 1 expandable to 4 million
items.quote: We are also establishing a rotary compressor manufacturing facility at our Supa plant. Machinery has been ordered. Installation is planned to begin in August 2026 and operations are expected to commence by quarter 4 of FY27. We will have a capacity of 2 million compressors in the first phase, which can be expanded to 4 million compressors in the second phase.

items.statement: Expanded washing machine facility at Greater Noida now operational with strong order book visibility
items.quote: Our expanded washing machine facility is now operational at Greater Noida. We have strong order book visibility and outsourcing momentum in the semi-automatic segment continues to build.

items.statement: Consolidating molding facilities at Salarpur, Rajasthan, campus ready by July-August 2026, multiyear cost structure improvement showing in margins over FY27 and FY28
items.quote: We are consolidating some of our molding facilities at Salarpur, Rajasthan, which will help us in enhancing our operational performance, space utilization, eliminating warehouse leases and allowing us to build better economies of scale.

items.statement: RAC industry declined approximately 15% in FY26 due to three demand shocks: prolonged monsoon, GST rate cut announcement, BEE rating transition anticipation, and weak consumer sentiment
items.quote: The RAC industry, which remains the largest contributor to our product revenues, experienced a decline of approximately 15% during FY26.

items.statement: Channel inventory normalized materially from peak of ~5 million units in FY26, April-May showing better sellout momentum vs last year
items.quote: Channel inventory have now normalized materially from the peak of approximately 5 million units seen during FY26. April and May have shown better sellout momentum compared to the same period last year.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 EBITDA declined 43% to INR131.5 crores, net profit down 56% to INR64.2 crores due to LPG crisis, truck shortage, commodity inflation, currency depreciation and negative operating leverage
items.quote: EBITDA came in at INR131.5 crores compared to INR231.72 crores last year, which was a decline of 43%. Net profit for the quarter was INR64.2 crores versus INR146.39 crores and a decline of 56% for the quarter.

items.statement: Full year FY26 EBITDA INR441.76 crores vs INR519.16 crores, PAT INR193.61 crores vs INR290.92 crores, margin compression from input cost inflation, negative operating leverage, elevated finance costs
items.quote: Full year consolidated revenues are INR5,288 crores versus INR4,869 crores in the last financial year. EBITDA stood at INR441.76 crores versus INR519.16 crores and profit after tax stood at INR193.61 crores versus INR290.92 crores last year.

items.statement: Industry implemented cumulative price hikes of 10-15% from Dec'25 to Apr'26 but weak demand and excess inventory constrained pass-through, suppressing gross margins
items.quote: Since December '25 till April '26, the industry implemented cumulative price hike of around 10% to 15%, but with weak demand and excess inventory in the channel, the ability to fully pass through these increases remain constrained, suppressing gross margins across the entire value chain.

items.statement: Company took price increases of 10-12% overall but rupee depreciation and commodity inflation not fully passed through, exchange rate volatility remains key risk
items.quote: We would have also taken a price increase of anywhere between 10% to 12% till now. From the last year basis on our overall numbers. But as Vishal ji was explaining, there are -- is a rupee, which has depreciated very sharply and some of those payments are made generally slightly later.

items.statement: Indian rupee depreciated ~20% against USD Y-o-Y, substantially inflating input costs; copper, aluminum, plastics and key components rose sharply
items.quote: Most significantly, the Indian rupee depreciated approximately 20% against the U.S. dollar on a Y-o-Y basis, substantially inflating our input costs.

items.statement: Forex loss of INR38.77 crores in FY26 vs gain of INR17.99 crores in FY25; Q4 forex loss INR25.82 crores vs gain of INR12.77 crores, driven by unhedged liabilities mark-to-market at INR94.8/USD
items.quote: For the full year FY26, our forex loss was INR38.77 crores versus a forex gain of about INR17.99 crores in FY25. Even for the quarter, we had a forex loss of about INR25.82 crores versus a gain of INR12.77 crores last year same quarter.

items.statement: Room AC revenue declined 12% Y-o-Y in Q4 to INR1,210 crores but grew 9% full year; washing machine business grew 52% full year and 70% in Q4; cooler business declined 10.8% in Q4 and 8.2% full year
items.quote: Room AC revenue declined 12% Y-o-Y to INR1,210 crores. For the full year, RAC revenue grew 9% year-on-year. The washing machine business grew phenomenally 52% on a full year basis. And for the quarter, it grew at about 70%. Cooler business saw a decline of about 10.8% for the quarter And on an even full year basis, there was a decline of 8.2% in the cooler business.

items.statement: Continue to gain wallet share within anchor customers and deepen trust with brand partners, benefiting from structural shift towards outsourcing in Indian consumer durable manufacturing
items.quote: We continue to gain wallet share within our anchor customers and deepen our trust with our brand partners and continue to benefit from the structural shift towards outsourcing in the Indian consumer global manufacturing.

items.statement: Working capital stressed in FY26 due to higher inventory carried through Q4 and stretched receivable cycles, leading to higher borrowing and interest cost; expecting significant improvement in FY27
items.quote: During the full year, working capital was stressed mainly because of the higher inventory, which we carried and the demand washout, which happened in the first quarter last year, and we carried the higher inventory through the Q4.

items.statement: Inventory at end of March INR1,600 crores (AC business INR1,300 crores including INR450 crores finished goods); targeting reduction to less than INR900 crores by June end
items.quote: We had an inventory of close to INR1,600 crores at the end of March quarter, out of which the AC business alone was having close to INR1,300 crores of inventory and rest of the other businesses had about INR300-odd crores.

items.statement: FY26 production ~1.75 million AC sets plus 200,000-300,000 extra IDUs; annual AC capacity ~4.5 million, average utilization 45-50%
items.quote: See our overall production in FY26 was around 1.75 million sets, okay? And we make -- normally, we make some extra IDUs for some customers who take IDUs, extra, which should be around 250,000 to 300,000 for the whole year.

items.statement: PLI income INR37.5 crores for FY25 received; FY26 PLI INR71 crores (including NGM PLI) to be received and recognized in FY27
items.quote: total amount will be INR71 crores. Tanay Shah: INR71 crores for FY... Pramod Gupta: The amount is for FY26, which we will be receiving in '27 and recognizing in '27

items.statement: Exchange rate volatility is key risk - rupee at 94-95.5, factored up to 97, but beyond that becomes problem for everyone; last year PLI target desperation may create industry pricing pressure
items.quote: Today, we are sitting at maybe 94, 95.5 something. It can go up to INR97. This is what we factored in. But it goes beyond that, then it becomes a problem for everyone.

items.statement: LPG shortage from Gulf conflict forced 2-week plant shutdowns in March, retrofit to alternative fuel at exorbitant cost, reverse labor migration and truck shortages disrupted ramp-up
items.quote: Then in March, which is historically our single largest production month of the year, we were hit by a shortage of commercial LPG arising from the Gulf conflict. This forced nearly 2-week plant shutdowns to retrofit our operations to alternative fuel sources at a very exorbitant cost.

items.statement: Completed migration to SAP in FY26, improving inventory visibility, demand planning and financial reporting accuracy; implemented comprehensive cost management program
items.quote: During FY26, we have completed our migration to SAP. This has improved our inventory visibility, demand planning and financial reporting accuracy. This is very important as we scale up our operations.

items.statement: Medium-term revenue target of INR600 crores remains reference point, achievable through volume growth, high-value products, and railway contributions
items.quote: As we enter financial year 2027, the medium-term revenu e target of INR600 crores remains our reference point. We believe it is achievable through a com bination of volume growth from existing OEM customers, scaling high-value products, and rail ways beginning to contribute

items.quote: And we believe that this growth because trajectory shall continue not in this stage it's also recouping of the last years -- last 2 years of business that we had lost. items.statement: Working capital expected to improve further in FY27
items.quote: This improvement is in line with our guidance of working capital improvement, and we further expect it to improve in FY27.

items.statement: Stand-alone tax rate expected around 25% going forward

items.statement: No major capex envisaged in near future; maintenance capex INR50-75 crores annually
items.quote: I would say around about INR50-odd crores of maintenance capex. items.statement: FY26 capex of INR315 crores completed; all plants commercialized
items.quote: During the year, we did capex of INR315 crores towards the last leg of the capex program. And with that, all our plants are commercialized.

items.statement: Current gross block can support peak revenue of INR3,500 crores
items.quote: Ankur we should be looking at about INR3,500 crores kind of a number from this revenue -- sorry, from this block at least.

items.quote: So, if you look at my order book, order book itself is around about INR14,000 crores. I believe that's the kind of a number I would really go with for now. And I think that's the number that going forward on an outlook basis also, I'm more comfortable with.

items.statement: Pharma and polymer segments expected to be margin accretive versus agrochemicals

items.statement: Consolidated working capital at 215-220 days pro forma; stand-alone at 240-250 days; trajectory improving

items.statement: Operating cash flow of INR334 crores in FY26; stand-alone INR274 crores
items.quote: We have delivered operating cash flow of INR334 crores during FY '26 on the back of improved asset utilization, operational efficiency and better working capital management.
