items.statement: Bliss acquisition funded via INR300 crores NCDs and non-controlling, non-voting equity instruments
items.quote: The transaction will be funded through a combination of approximately INR300 crores via non-convertible debentures and non-controlling, non-voting equity instruments for the balance consideration.

items.statement: Definitive agreement to acquire 43.3-48.2% of Bliss GVS Pharma plus open offer for up to 26%
items.quote: We are pleased to also announce that we have entered into a definitive agreement to acquire 43.3% to 48.2% equity stake along with an open offer of up to 26% additional shares to public shareholders of Bliss GVS Pharma Limited.

items.statement: Jayhawk acquisition completed; 1 month 2 days consolidated in FY26; pro forma revenue ~US$76M
items.quote: Jayhawk reported a pro forma annual revenue of approximately US$76 million, reflecting the strong scale and capabilities of the platform. I would also like to highlight that in the current financial, we have consolidated only 1 month and 2 days of Jayhawk performance.

items.statement: Bliss GVS pro forma revenue INR927 crores; capacity utilization 30%, target 60-70% near-medium term
items.quote: Also, if you look at this company is today having an operating capacity utilization of only 30% and we believe that, that can be very quickly enhanced to 60% to 70% in the near to medium term, and that's something which we would be looking at leveraging.

items.statement: Pro forma consolidated revenue >INR4,000 crores and EBITDA ~INR834 crores across Anupam, Tanfac, Jayhawk, Bliss
items.quote: Coming to the top line on a pro forma basis, if I were to look at the pro forma basis business across the 4 companies, Anupam should be -- today is around INR1,676 crores, Tanfac INR711 crores, Jayhawk is roughly INR722 crores, depending on the exchange rate that you take. And Bliss is INR927 crores. So total, if I look at as of today delivered business on a pro forma basis, we should be looking a

items.statement: FY26 stand-alone revenue mix: Agro 55%, Pharma 20%, Performance Materials 18%, Personal Care 7%
items.quote: Our business vertical-wise revenue on a stand-alone basis for FY26 is as follows: Agrochemical segment contributed 55% of our revenue, Pharma segment contributed 20% of our revenue, Performance Materials contributed 18% of our revenue and balance was 7% contributed by Personal Care.

items.statement: High-performance materials revenue grew 3x from INR97 crores (FY22) to INR305 crores (FY26); Pharma grew 15x from INR21 crores to INR339 crores
items.quote: On a stand-alone basis, our revenue from high-performance materials increased threefold from INR97 crores in FY '22 to INR305 crores in FY '26, while Pharma revenue has grown 15-fold from INR21 crores in FY '22 to INR339 crores in FY '26.

items.statement: Added multiple multinational customers and 3 new products in FY26
items.quote: During the year, we added multiple multinational customers, expanded our product portfolio with three new product additions, further strengthening our presence across high-value specialty chemical segments.

items.statement: Common and complementary customers exist across Anupam, Jayhawk, and Bliss; cross-pollination expected
items.quote: So first, on Jayhawk, yes, there are common customers, which are there and there are common significant customers as well and common -- and there are complementary customers also. So there are few new customers that Jayhawk will offer to us where we can showcase our product and our services and offerings

items.statement: FY26 consolidated revenue INR2,384 crores (+65% YoY); EBITDA INR543 crores (23% margin); PAT INR222 crores (9% margin)
items.quote: Revenue from operations was at INR2,384 crores as compared to INR1,448 crores in FY25, up 65% Y-o-Y. EBITDA, including other income, was at INR543 crores as compared to INR412 crores in FY25. This translates to an EBITDA margin of 23% for

items.statement: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue INR639 crores (+26% YoY); EBITDA INR141 crores (22% margin); PAT INR56 crores (9% margin)
items.quote: Total income was at INR639 crores as compared to INR506 crores in Q4 FY25, up 26% Y-o-Y. EBITDA, including other income, was at INR141 crores as compared to INR150 crores in Q4 FY25, translating to an EBITDA margin of 22% for this quarter.

items.statement: Bliss acquisition timeline 2-3 months subject to SEBI approval and open offer results
items.quote: First, the time line, if you look at it is basically if you depend upon the SEBI approval and the open offer results. So anything between 2 to 3 months of time frame is what we estimate today, but that's an estimation.

items.statement: Bliss Halol capex of INR250 crores for CDMO project with large multinational pharma player; separate from existing plants
items.quote: That capex is basically for the CDMO business, which has been offered by a very large multinational pharma player, existing customers of theirs. And so it's a separate capex for a separate objective and separate business vertical.

items.statement: Bliss existing professional management to continue; Anupam to guide and support; promoters relinquishing control
items.quote: First, the business on a stand-alone basis shall run from their management and be guided and supported by Anupam. Okay? The shareholder and the promoter are relinquishing their control and their shareholding.

items.statement: Anupam has no Africa exposure; Bliss has significant Africa presence; complementary geographic strength
items.quote: So first, Anupam right now has no exposure to that geography. I believe that company's Bliss' exposure. Yes, they are. We understand they're largely there. But that's one part of the synergy of the business that we were talking about.

items.statement: Tanfac backward integration secures hydrofluoric acid and potassium fluoride; new products and customers being added
items.quote: Our investment in Tanfac Industries has significantly strengthened our fluorination platform by securing uninterrupted access to critical raw materials such as hydrofluoric acid and potassium fluoride. Further with support of Anupam, Tanfac is in the process of introducing new products as well as new customers in this financial year.

items.statement: FY27 guidance: sales volume 5-5.5 msf, sales value INR3,300-3,500 cr, collections INR2,100-2,200 cr, handovers 3,750-3,800 units, pipeline addition 7-8 msf, GDV addition INR5,000-6,000 cr
items.value: sales volume 5-5.5 msf; sales value INR3,300-3,500 cr; collections INR2,100-2,200 cr; handovers 3,750-3,800 units; pipeline addition 7-8 msf; GDV addition INR5,000-6,000 cr
items.quote: Based on current visibility, management expects FY '27 performance to be stronger than FY '26. Our guidance includes sales volume of 5 -5.5 million square feet during FY '27, sales value of INR3,300 -3,500 crores, collections of INR2,100 - 2,200 crores, handovers of 3,750 - 3,800 units, pipeline addition of 7-8 million square feet, GDV addition of INR5,000-6,000 crores.

items.statement: FY26 sales value INR2,354 cr, sales volume 4.15 msf, collections INR1,661 cr (+12% YoY), handovers 3,465 units (+10% YoY)
items.quote: For FY '26, sales value for the year stood at INR2,354 crores, registering a marginal increase over the previous year despite delays in certain project launches. Sales volume of 4.1 5 million square feet. Collection reached all -time high of INR1,661 crores, growing 12% year -on-year. Customer handover reached 3,465 units, up 10% over the previous year.

items.statement: FY26 revenue INR1,357 cr (+39% YoY), gross profit INR365 cr (+47% YoY), gross margin stable at 29%, EBITDA INR177 cr (flat YoY), net profit INR101 cr (+30% YoY)
items.quote: Revenue increased by 39% to INR1,357 crores. Gross profit increased by 47% to INR365 crores. EBITDA stood at INR177 crores. Net profit increased by 30% to INR101 crores, crossing the INR100 crores mark for the first time.

items.statement: FY26 new project investment INR372 cr (highest annual); FY27 new project investment expected INR350-400 cr for 8 msf pipeline addition
items.quote: So that 8 million addition would mean anywhere between INR350 crores- INR400 crores of capital commitment.

items.statement: 16.7 msf ongoing projects (85% sold), 2.6 msf unsold ongoing, 18.6 msf upcoming pipeline, total unsold potential >21 msf with GDV ~INR13,950 cr; FY27 launch pipeline ~7 msf across 4 cities
items.quote: We currently have 16.7 million square feet under ongoing projects, of which 85% has already been sold. Along with 2.6 million square feet of unsold area of ongoing projects and an additional 18.6 million square feet of the upcoming pipeline, total unsold development potential is over 21 million square feet, representing GDV of nearly INR13,950 crores.

items.statement: Construction cost inflation limited: cement, steel, RMC stable; tiles, paints, PVC windows seeing 5-10% cost pressure but cushioned in project budgets; market price upside limited to 5-6% annually
items.quote: The markets are looking at not more than 5% - 6% annual upside in the existing projects or the market pricing increase is not more than 5%- 6%. That will cover an inflationary pressure of what 8% to 10% in the construction cost side.

items.statement: FY26 operating inflow INR1,049 cr, cash from operations INR271 cr, free cash flow before new investment INR224 cr; FY27 construction spend expected INR900-1,000 cr
items.quote: For FY '26, operating inflow reached to INR1,049 crores. Cash flow from operations stood at INR271 crores. Free cash flow before new project investment was INR224 crores.

items.statement: FY27 revenue recognition potential INR1,740 cr from 3.8 msf completions; FY28 Mission 1-2-3-4 targets: sales INR5,000 cr, revenue INR2,500 cr, PBT INR250 cr
items.quote: We expect approximately 3.8 million square feet of project completions during the year, creating a revenue recognition potential of nearly INR1,740 crores and handovers of over 3,500 units.

items.statement: FY26 launches saw 30-85% inventory sold at launch: Spectrum Pune 300+ units, Songs of Earth Bangalore 85%, Skybloom Villas Kolkata 50%, Signature Square Kolkata 40%
items.value: Spectrum Pune 300+ units; Songs of Earth 85%; Skybloom Villas 50%; Signature Square 40%
items.quote: This includes Spectrum, Pune, over 300 units sold during launch year; Songs of the Earth, Bangalore over 85% sold in launch y ear; Skybloo m Villas, Kolkata over 50% sold, Signature Square in Kolkata, approximately 40% sold at launch.

items.statement: Kolkata land matter amicably resolved with Government of West Bengal, surrender of 42 acres, 2.3 msf apartment approval secured, 100+ acres remaining for monetization
items.quote: One of the key achievement during the year was the amicable resolution of long -pending land matter in Kolkata. The settlement and conveying process have significantly enhanced the monetization potential of our land bank and are expected to unlock value in an accelerated manner.

items.statement: Key risks: IT sector employment trends, affordability pressure from interest rates, extended sales cycles, approval delays, OC receipt, BD pipeline conversion; mitigated by mid/upper-mid segment focus, diversified markets, calibrated pricin
items.quote: At the sector level, factors such as IT sector employment trends, affordability pressure arising from the interest rates and extended sales cycles warrant close monitoring. We also remain focused on execution -related risk, particularly timely approval, receipt of occupancy certificates, and conversion of our BD pipeline into launches.

items.statement: New product testing in Kolkata: villas (launched FY26, strong), plotted development (launched FY27), commercial (launched recently); recalibrating strategy for 100+ acres based on plot/villa/commercial performance
items.quote: We launched the Villa project late last year, last fiscal. And that was, again, a new product. Villa was never launched in this micro market. We don't have any villa projects in the micro market that we operate. Therefore, we started well, did very well. Similarly, plotted development, branded plotte d development is not a common thing in the micro market that we are operating. Therefore, we wante

items.statement: Mid-market and mid-premium demand strong in core markets (Bangalore, Pune, Chennai, Kolkata) supported by rising incomes, urbanization, end-user demand; branded developer preference increasing
items.quote: Demand in the mid-market and mid -premium segment remains strong, supported by rising incomes, urbanization and sustained end user demand. Importantly, our core markets, Bangalore, Pune, Chennai and Kolkata continue to exhibit healthy economic activity and favorable housing demand fundamentals.

items.statement: May use intermittent debt to bridge timing gap between completed project cash flows and new land commitments; no diversion of ongoing project collections to land acquisition
items.quote: We might embark on an intermittent debt to support any bridge that is req uired between the profit generation or the cash flow , our share of cash flow being realized versus capital commitment being made on the land part.

items.statement: No management changes mentioned; CEO Gopalakrishnan and CFO Ravindra Pandey led the call with CMD Murali
items.quote: Myself, along with our CEO and CMD will be glad to answer all your queries.

items.statement: Management expects to maintain or improve margins and grow at a similar trajectory over the next 2-3 years, but declines to give specific FY27 margin or revenue guidance.
items.quote: I wish I could guide you at this point in time. But you know how the situation is. But on our side, internally, if you ask us, we definitely want to do better than what we have done over the next two to three years.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin was 18.3% and PAT margin 13.6%, with gross margin at 70.5% (76% excluding scanners).
items.quote: EBITDA and PAT margins for the quarter were recorded at a healthy level of 18.3% and 13.6% respectively. The improvement in the margin is despite a half-quarter impact of US tariff, weighing on our EBITDA margin by around 74 bps.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin was 15.6% and PAT margin 10.4%.
items.quote: EBITDA margins stood at 15.6% and PAT recorded 10.4% for the year.

items.statement: Dental lab business recorded highest ever quarterly revenue of Rs 45.9 crore, up 27% YoY, driven by domestic recovery and highest ever international revenue.
items.quote: Our dental lab business recorded its highest ever quarterly revenue of Rs. 45.9 crore with a growth of 27% year-on-year. This growth was driven by a strong recovery in the domestic business coupled with the highest ever revenue from our international operations.

items.statement: International lab business grew 40.9% YoY; US tariff impact normalized in latter half of Q4.
items.quote: Our international lab business delivered a robust growth of 40.9% YOY. In USA, we continued to absorb higher tariff cost in the first half of the quarter which was normalized in the latter half.

items.statement: Domestic lab business grew 16.3% YoY to Rs 23.7 crore.
items.quote: Speaking of domestic business, it delivered a solid growth of 16.3% year-on-year. We were able to sail through near-term headwinds in this business and delivered revenues of Rs. 23.7 crores.

items.statement: Bizdent aligner business grew 10.9% YoY in Q4; Vedia aligner raw material revenue was Rs 7.3 crore, stable sequentially but impacted by higher March freight costs.
items.quote: Bizdent, our clear aligner business in India, witnessed a meaningful recovery from the previous quarter and recorded a healthy growth of 10.9% on YOY basis. Vedia, our aligner raw metal business, remained stable sequentially and reported a revenue of Rs. 7.3 crores.

items.statement: Kids-e-Dental pediatric business revenue was Rs 5.4 crore in Q4.
items.quote: Speaking of our pediatric dental business, Kids-e-Dental, the revenue stood for the quarter at Rs. 5.4 crores.

items.statement: Digital penetration in domestic lab is ~80%, targeting over 90% medium-term; each scanner placed drives long-term lab and aligner revenue.
items.quote: Now, our digital penetration in the domestic lab business stands at around 80% and we are targeting over 90% digital penetration over the medium-term. Each scanner placed is a long-term revenue driver for our laboratory and aligners.

items.statement: FY26 capex was ~Rs 18.4 crore; FY27 capex will be deployed from IPO proceeds based on operational capabilities and revenue growth.
items.quote: We have done a CAPEX of around Rs. 18.4 crores in FY '26. Our cash and bank balance including investments stood at around Rs. 99 crores.

items.statement: FY27 capex plan: will deploy IPO proceeds based on operational capabilities and revenue growth.
items.quote: Yes, we have the IPO proceeds still with us in terms of CAPEX. We have done, like Dharmesh bhai said, about Rs. 18 crores last year. So, we plan to deploy CAPEX based on the operational capabilities. So, we see the revenues growing and based on that, we will keep balancing out CAPEX.

items.statement: Export revenue share is 33-34%; US is 20% of revenue, currently at 10% tariff (down from 50%), not a deal-breaker.
items.quote: Export revenue is about 33%-34%.

items.statement: US revenue is 20% of total; tariff now at 10% vs 50% earlier, management sees no issue for medium to long term.
items.quote: Currently, the US percentage is 20% of our revenue. And, at 10%, the situation is, I would say better than 50%. But before it was zero to us. So, there is still some percentage. But I think the US has done well, if you look at a number, the US has done well. And we don't see any situation of why it should not keep doing well for the next few years.

items.statement: Scanner deployments: 211 units in Q4 FY26, 1,009 units in FY26.
items.quote: 211, on a yearly basis, 1009.

items.statement: Bizdent aligner pricing pressure eased in Q4; management prioritizes margin preservation over volume, will evaluate balanced approach going forward.
items.quote: But we wanted on our side as management to preserve the margins. And I think we have done that. That is what it shows. And like you said, we have seen recovery back in Q4. And we are confident that as we move forward, we will keep evaluating whether in terms of putting pressure on the pricing versus margins and growing.

items.statement: Management acknowledges funded competitors but highlights Rs 99 crore cash reserves and focus on innovation, digitization, and automation to win market share.
items.quote: See, competition, Ajay, have been since 35 years of us doing business. Was there competition or not? The answer is yes. 20 years later, will there be competition? The answer is yes. So, that will never change. You know, in the past, probably non funded competitors and now funded competitors. But we are also funding, we are sitting with Rs. 99 crores in hand. So, we know how to deploy, where to dep

items.statement: Heartland Dental is a key US DSO partner but revenue is diversified; no contract changes due to tariffs; adding more DSOs but not disclosing specifics.
items.quote: So, I think to your question number one, there has been no change. In fact, like I said, the situation has become better than what it was 50% to 10%. So, we don't see any challenge for the U.S. business. And regarding adding DSOs, I think even if we add probably will not call out in a calls.

items.statement: Dentists know the company as 'Illusion' brand; currently serve 22,000 dentists for lab and 5,000-7,000 for aligners out of 3 lakh total in India.
items.quote: Dentists in India know us as Illusion. So, whether it is Illusion Dental, which is our lab or Illusion aligners, which is our aligner business. So, if you ask for that, they would have heard the name, if they are doing business or not, like I said, today we are doing business with 22,000 dentists and aligners, there are maybe 5,000- 6,000, - 7,000 dentists, India has 3 lakh dentists.

items.statement: Kids-e-Dental international registrations (EU/US) are in active phase but timelines are unpredictable and not disclosed until achieved.
items.quote: I think the question to the potential is very good. Coming back to the timeline, I think in the past we have tried. But again, this is all regulatory bodies. So, it's very, very hard to predict. They give us a timeline. We probably call out a timeline. Sometimes it happens, sometimes it doesn't happen. Because that's completely out of our control.

items.statement: Management keeps eyes open for acquisitions/IP/tech that add value; will announce only after completion.
items.quote: I can't give you all the details. But what we can tell you is since day 1, when we started the business or even today post our IPO, we always keep our eyes and ears open. If there is an opportunity, we will decide. We will see if it brings value to Laxmi Dental, we will go ahead with the opportunity. When, which sector, what type of situation that we will call out once it's done and not before tha

items.statement: Company remains debt-free; finance costs dropped to Rs 0.3 crore in Q4 from Rs 1.3 crore YoY.
items.quote: Finance costs for the quarter stood at Rs. 0.3 crores compared to Rs. 1.3 crores last year. The company remains debt-free.

items.statement: Other expenses included an ECL credit of Rs 91 lakhs in Q4 FY26.
items.quote: Other expenses for the quarter stood at Rs. 11.9 crores as compared to Rs. 13.8 crores in the corresponding period last year. It includes an ECL credit of Rs. 91 lakhs in Q4 FY '26.

items.statement: iScope 360 launched: remote scanning, oral health tracking, virtual consultation; device retailed at ~Rs 2,000 with subscription points model for dentists.
items.quote: So, there is the revenue is first to sell the scope. So, the scope is currently retailed at about Rs. 2000. So, that the dentist can sell to the patient at a retail price, and we will give it to the dentist. So, it is dentist driven.

items.statement: Employee costs stable sequentially at Rs 26.8 crore in Q4, up 9.6% YoY; investing in automation and digital dentistry to keep people cost disproportional to sales growth.
items.quote: Employee costs for the quarter stood at Rs. 26.8 crores, remaining stable sequentially and registering a YOY increase of 9.6%.

items.statement: US tariff volatility, West Asia conflict, labor code transitions, and global freight cost spikes cited as key external headwinds in FY26.
items.quote: Our annual performance is especially noteworthy as it was delivered amid a challenging global environment marked by US tariff volatility, intensifying competition in the domestic aligner segment, labor code transitions and several other external headwinds during FY '26.

items.statement: Launched iScope 360 AI-connected remote dental platform for remote scanning, monitoring, oral health tracking, and virtual consultation.
items.quote: And lastly, launched a new AI-connected remote dental platform known as iScope 360. Dentistry is evolving drastically and has reached a stage where presence is not limited to a dental chair. The product iScope 360 offers a remote scanning, real-time monitoring, oral health tracking, and virtual consultation without a physical clinic visit.

items.statement: Management guides for approximately 30% CAGR in value terms over the next two to three years, with potential to exceed if gold prices remain stable.
items.quote: We remain committed to our guidance of delivering approximately 30% growth over the next two to three years.

items.statement: Volume growth of approximately 15% achieved in FY26; targeting 30-35% volume growth if gold prices remain steady.
items.quote: If gold prices remain steady at current levels, we believe we can further accelerate this 15% volume growth to reach levels of 30% or even 35% in the near future.

items.statement: Manufacturing capacity expanded from 2,500 kgs to 4,000 kgs in Q4 FY26; blended capacity for FY26 was 2,625 kgs with 87% utilization.
items.quote: Firstly, we executed a major expansion of our manufacturing capabilities during the fourth quarter, resulting in a meaningful increase in production capacity from 2,500 kgs to 4,000 kgs.

items.statement: Installed capacity stays at 4,000 kgs for FY27; production expected to ramp up further in coming quarters.
items.quote: For the next financial year, our available installed capacity stays at 4,000 kgs, and we expect to further ramp up production in the coming quarters.

items.statement: Strategic entry into bridal jewellery segment; initial sales commenced through partners Tanishq and Malabar Gold and Diamonds.
items.quote: Secondly, we made a strategic entry into the bridal jewellery segment, which represents a natural extension to our core mangalsutra business.

items.statement: Bridal jewellery could contribute approximately one-third of revenue in current year; expected to match or surpass mangalsutra revenue within three years.
items.quote: Within this current year, approximately one-third of our revenue could be derived from the bridal segment. Looking ahead over the next three years, we anticipate the bridal segment growing to be on par with our Mangalsutra business or perhaps even surpassing it.

items.statement: Malabar Gold contributes 17% of revenue (~0.7 tonnes); Titan processes similar volume (~0.7 tonnes) but on job-work basis so value not comparable.
items.quote: 17% of our revenue is from our business with Malabar Gold. And we cannot compare Titan with them because Titan is completely based on job work.

items.statement: Birla, Reliance, and Indriya converted from job work to outright sales; negotiations ongoing with Tanishq for similar conversion.
items.quote: Definitely, today Birla is converted from job work to outright, Reliance is converted to job work to outright, and Indriya also Birla's that is also converted into outright. And Tata is we are currently operational. We are in the negotiations with Tanishq as well for conversion of job work into outright.

items.statement: Job work revenue INR28 cr in FY26; converting same volume to outright sales could generate 2-3x profit (INR70-80 cr top line potential per client).
items.quote: Our job work, the revenue we have generated amounts to INR28 crores; if we were to convert this into outright sales, it could potentially reach INR70 crores to INR80 crores.

items.statement: Hedging notional loss due to rising gold prices was the biggest driver of higher other expenses in Q4; ~60% of production hedged (30% barter, 17% GML, 13% MCX).
items.quote: The biggest difference, if any, is the hedging notional loss. Since we hedge gold, it results in a notional loss because if we have hedged the gold at whatever price we have bought it at in MCX, whatever additional payment we have to make due to increase in the price of gold, that actually results in loss.

items.statement: Debt-equity ratio 0.27; inventory churn 5x; working capital increased to support revenue growth; shift to outright sales will increase working capital needs but improve cash flow predictability.
items.quote: We have an debt-equity ratio of 0.27 and we have a churning of five times. So we have a churning for five times and for -- we require to so we increase our revenue and that's why we have a require our working capital.

items.statement: Targeting cash flow positive within approximately two quarters by converting labor-based engagements to outright contracts with organized players who have reliable payment cycles.
items.quote: Within approximately two quarters, we will have converted a significant portion of our operations. Therefore, as we engage with corporates specifically with all the organized players in the sector if we transition our existing labor-based engagements with them to an outright contractual basis, our transformation from the unorganized to the organized sector will accelerate commensurately.

items.statement: Wedding volumes increasing 7-8% annually; one crore weddings this year; gold jewellery demand escalating proportionally.
items.quote: Thus, with the volume of weddings increasing by approximately 7% to 8% annually, the gold jewellery industry is also advancing and expanding at a corresponding pace.

items.statement: Gold import duty raised from 6% to 15%; increase absorbed into market price; no distinct adverse impact as duty applies equally to buying and selling.
items.quote: When the duty rate increases say, to 15% that increase typically gets absorbed into the prevailing market price of gold. For instance, when the base price was INR150,000, and the duty hike was announced, the price of gold immediately rose to approximately INR160,000, reflecting the 9% increase.

items.statement: Revenue INR2,245.8 cr (+57.1% YoY); sales volume 500 kgs in Q4 (+16% YoY); blended capacity utilization 87% for FY26.
items.quote: For the full year, revenue from operation stood at INR2,245.8 crores, marking an increase of 57.1% Y-o-Y.

items.statement: Corporate clients contribute 49% of revenue, non-corporate 51%; 1,333 clients across India and world for mangalsutra.
items.quote: For the full year, the revenue contribution from the corporate clients stood at 49% and non-corporate clients at 51%.

items.statement: New factory built with new machinery and technology installed; capital expenditure reflected in higher other expenses.
items.quote: And recently you must have known that we have built new factories, so we had to make some expenditure to install some machinery and all that new technology in that factory as per the new factory.

items.statement: Gold price CAGR 10.9% over 42 years per RBI; rupee depreciation and global gold prices driving domestic price increases.
items.quote: Reflecting this, as per RBI, gold prices have delivered a CAGR of 10.9% over the last 42 years, increasing from 1,858 in 1983 to 1,52,228 as on April 15, 2026.

items.statement: Hedging notional losses occur when gold prices rise above hedged levels; ~60% of production hedged via barter, GML, and MCX.
items.quote: Since we hedge gold, it results in a notional loss because if we have hedged the gold at whatever price we have bought it at in MCX, whatever additional payment we have to make due to increase in the price of gold, that actually results in loss.

items.statement: New branch office inaugurated in Pune, expanding geographic footprint from Marathwada to Vidarbha regions in Western India.
items.quote: As a part of our ongoing expansion strategy, we successfully inaugurated a new branch office in Pune, a move that has significantly enhanced our geographic footprint in Western India from Marathwada to Vidarbha regions.

items.statement: Granite revenue growth target 10-12% YoY for FY27
items.quote: 10% to 13% is the consistent growth is what we are expecting on the Granite segment. We have witnessed little better growth in the previous years, but no, on the pessimistic side, if we estimate the number also, 10% to 12% is the number growth is what we can see.

items.statement: Quartz Phase 1 target 60% capacity utilization in FY27
items.quote: I think our endeavour is to reach at leas t 60% of the rated capacity this year. And you'll see a quarter-on-quarter improvement, yes

items.statement: Quartz Phase 1 revenue target INR400 crores in 3 years
items.quote: Now that could give top line of close to around INR400 crores. That is the number we are looking to target.

items.statement: Sri Lanka HMS Phase 1 revenue target INR350-400 crores in 3-4 years
items.quote: HMS in Sri Lanka, which will be operational by then, will give another INR350 crores to INR400 crores. And that is on Phase 1.

items.statement: KMML commercial plant revenue target INR200 crores
items.quote: KMML project once it's commercialized, I think ther e also we're looking at a revenue of close to INR200 crores

items.statement: Overall revenue target 2.5x in 3-4 years reaching ~INR2,100 crores
items.quote: So, basically, if you look at the overall thing at that point of time, you're looking at INR1,000 crores in granite, then about IN R1,100 crores around that from these 3 projects that we just

items.statement: Quartz Phase 2 capex INR125-130 crores, commissioning Q4 FY27
